- Install **dedicated small electron-gun purity monitors** (Redus/Berkeley design with α-source electron injectors) at multiple vertical positions — enables real-time drift-velocity and lifetime maps, not just single-point measurements

**Cryogenic vacuum jacketing improvement**
- Upgrade to **multilayer insulation (MLI) with 60-layer blanket** inside vacuum jacket; add **LN₂ cold trap on the vacuum space** to cryopump residual organics that outgas into LXe

---

## 4. Cathode High Voltage Delivery

### Problem
Earlier detectors limited drift field to ~0.5–1 kV/cm due to HV feedthrough discharge risks, constraining NR/ER discrimination at low energies.

### Upgrades

**Custom HV feedthrough**
- Replace standard SHV coaxial feedthroughs with **PTFE-sleeve, graded-field feedthroughs** capable of **100+ kV DC in LXe** (designs developed by LUX/LZ groups)
- Use **ultra-pure polyimide (Kapton HN) or UHMWPE insulation** on internal HV cable — lower U/Th than standard coax dielectric
- Target **>3 kV/cm drift field** — dramatically improves electron-recoil/nuclear-recoil separation at energies below 10 keV_nr

---

## 5. Veto and Shielding Systems

### Problem
Earlier detectors used passive water/polyethylene shields without active tagging of Compton-scattered gammas or muon-induced neutrons.

### Upgrades

**Active Gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator (Gd-LS) veto**
- Surround the LXe cryostat with a **Gd-LS outer detector** (as implemented in LZ and XENONnT)
- Gd thermal neutron capture (n,γ) with ~8 MeV gamma cascade detected in Gd-LS — tags >95% of radiogenic neutrons that would otherwise fake NR signals
- Use **Gd-loaded pseudocumene at 0.1% Gd by mass**, instrumented with 8" PMTs (e.g., **Hamamatsu R5912**)
- Volume: ~17 tonnes provides >10 mean free paths for MeV gammas

**Muon veto**
- Install **water Cherenkov detector panels** or plastic scintillator paddles above and around the outer detector
- Coincidence logic with **<100 ns timing resolution** vetoes muon-induced neutron backgrounds

---

## 6. Data Acquisition and Trigger

### Problem
Earlier DAQ systems (e.g., 14-bit, 250 MSPS ADCs with hardware trigger thresholds) missed sub-keV signals and had dead time during large S2 events.

### Upgrades

**Continuous digitization with software triggering**
- Upgrade to **16-bit, 250 MSPS digitizers** (e.g., CAEN V1725 or equivalent) with **zero-suppression firmware**
- Implement **FPGA-based triggerless acquisition** — record all channels continuously, apply pulse-finding in software offline
- This recovers **S1 signals as small as 1–2 photons**, extending sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter and sub-keV NR

**Summed waveform channel**
- Add a **hardware analog sum channel** of all top-array channels for fast global trigger — reduces false trigger rate while maintaining efficiency >99% for S1 ≥ 3 photons

---

## 7. Calibration Source Delivery

### Problem
External gamma sources (⁶⁰Co, ²⁴¹AmBe) produce limited rate in fiducial volume and can't calibrate the low-energy NR band precisely.

### Upgrades

**Dissolved ⁸³ᵐKr and tritiated methane injection system**
- Install a **gas-phase capillary injection port** to introduce ⁸³ᵐKr (41.5 keV ER, distributed uniformly throughout LXe) — enables full 3D position-dependent light/charge yield calibration
- Add **tritiated methane (CH₃T) injection** for sub-10 keV ER calibration (endpoint 18.6 keV)
- Requires dedicated **cleanup loop with activated charcoal trap** to remove Kr/CH₃T post-calibration

**DD neutron generator**
- Install a compact **2.45 MeV DD neutron generator** (e.g., Adelphi DD-109) with collimator on the outer shielding — delivers mono-energetic neutrons for in-situ NR band calibration at known recoil energies

---

## Summary Priority Table

| Upgrade | Primary Performance Gain | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM photon detectors | +50–100% light yield, −10× background | High |
| Mesh/ITO electrodes | Better field uniformity, lower SE background | Medium |
| HV upgrade (>3 kV/cm) | Better ER/NR separation below 10 keV | Medium |
| Gd-LS outer detector | Neutron veto >95% | High |
| Continuous DAQ | Sub-keV threshold, no dead time | Medium |
| Getter upgrade | >10 ms lifetime, uniform S2 | Low-Medium |
| Kr/tritium calibration | Accurate low-E response model | Low |

---

The single highest-leverage upgrade is **replacing PMTs with cryogenic SiPM arrays**: it simultaneously improves light yield (improving energy threshold and ER/NR separation), dramatically reduces the dominant radioactive background source (the PMT glass), and enables a more compact detector geometry for a given fiducial mass.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Liquid Argon Neutrino Detector Prototype

## Framing the Problem

"Primary physics performance" for a LArTPC neutrino detector means: **energy resolution, spatial resolution, particle identification efficiency, signal-to-noise ratio, and neutrino interaction reconstruction fidelity**. I'll address each systematically with concrete hardware solutions.

---

## 1. Charge Readout System

### Current Typical Baseline
Wire planes (induction + collection) with ~3–5 mm wire pitch, cold analog front-end ASICs.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Pixel-based charge readout (LArPix architecture)**
- Replace wire planes with a fully 3D pixelated anode using the LArPix ASIC tiles (currently ~4.4 mm pixel pitch, push toward ~2–3 mm)
- Eliminates the wire plane ambiguity problem in track reconstruction — removes the inherent degeneracy in multi-track events that plagues 2D projective readout
- Concrete implementation: tile the anode plane with LArPix v2c or next-generation ASICs, bump-bonded to PCB tiles, daisy-chained via cold LVDS links
- Expected gain: ~40% improvement in multi-track vertex resolution, near-elimination of ghost track artifacts

**Charge-Light matched readout timing**
- Pair pixel tiles with embedded SiPM arrays (1 mm² Hamamatsu VUV4 or FBK NUV-HD-Cryo) at ~1 per 4 cm² for sub-100 ns t₀ tagging per interaction vertex rather than per-event
- This enables drift-coordinate precision of <1 mm rather than the ~few-mm from global light matching

**Lower noise front-end ASICs**
- Replace LArASIC-generation front ends with cold ADC designs running at 2 MHz sampling, ENC target <300 e⁻ (from current ~400–500 e⁻ typical)
- Specific target: SLAC/BNL cold ADC (65 nm CMOS process) qualified for 87 K operation
- Directly improves dE/dx resolution → better π/p/μ separation via Bragg peak reconstruction

---

## 2. Photon Detection System

### Current Typical Baseline
Bar-style ARAPUCA or dip-coated TPB light guides, ~1–2% photon detection efficiency (PDE) system-level.

### Proposed Upgrades

**X-ARAPUCA with dichroic filter optimization**
- Deploy second-generation X-ARAPUCA modules with improved dichroic filter transmission (>80% at 430 nm, <1% at 127 nm) and SiPM tile packing factor
- Use FBK VUV-HD3 SiPMs with measured PDE ~24% at 127 nm at 77 K
- Target system-level PDE: 3–5% (2–3× improvement over baseline)
- This directly improves energy resolution: δE/E scales roughly as 1/√N_photons

**Wavelength-shifting reflector foils on cathode and field cage**
- Line the cathode plane and inner field cage walls with 3M ESR + TPB-doped coating or PEN foil (polyethylene naphthalate, which is itself a VUV-to-visible shifter)
- PEN is self-shifting without secondary deposition — eliminates coating delamination risk at cryogenic temperatures
- Increases solid angle coverage effectively without adding active channels
- Estimated photon yield increase: 30–50% with full cathode + FC coverage

**Fast timing SiPMs for supernova burst tagging**
- For a prototype with supernova physics goals, add a dedicated fast-timing layer of SiPMs with <1 ns SPTR (single photon time resolution)
- Use SensL J-series or Hamamatsu S13360 series with cold-qualified quenching resistors
- Enables ~10 ns event timing → 10 μm-level drift reconstruction when combined with 500 ns electron drift times

---

## 3. High Voltage and Field Cage

### Current Typical Baseline
Resistive divider field cage, HV feedthrough at ~50–100 kV, field uniformity ~1% typical.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Field cage with embedded resistive shell (not discrete resistors)**
- Replace discrete resistor chains (failure-prone, non-uniform) with printed thick-film resistive traces on FR4-equivalent cryogenic PCB (e.g., Rogers 4350B tested to 87 K) or resistive kapton sheets
- Eliminates discrete solder joint failure modes — single most common cause of field cage failure in prototypes
- Enables tighter field uniformity: target <0.1% distortion over fiducial volume

**Modular HV feedthrough with in-situ monitoring**
- Replace single-point HV feedthrough with a design incorporating a cold-side capacitive voltage divider + readout ASIC to monitor actual cathode voltage in real time
- Use Kapton-encapsulated coaxial cable rated for 150 kV with UHMWPE outer jacket (tested to 77 K)
- Add Rogowski coil around cathode HV contact for microdischarge pulse detection → early warning of HV instability

**Greinacher (Cockcroft-Walton) cold HV multiplier option**
- For prototypes targeting very high drift fields (>1 kV/cm) over longer drift distances, a cold CW multiplier chain powered from a modest warm supply eliminates the need for high-voltage feedthrough rated above 100 kV
- Reduces risk of feedthrough failure — single largest cause of LAr detector downtime

---

## 4. Purity and Recirculation System

### Current Typical Baseline
Room-temperature Oxisorb/molecular sieve filtration, ~1–10 ppb O₂-equivalent impurity.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Cryogenic in-line getter system**
- Add a SAES MonoTorr or comparable metal getter operating at 400°C inline on the gas recirculation loop
- Target: <0.1 ppb O₂-equivalent (corresponds to electron lifetime >10 ms, enabling >3 m drift)
- This is the single most impactful upgrade for long-drift prototypes — doubling electron lifetime directly doubles the usable fiducial volume

**Dedicated cold recirculation pump (no warm return)**
- Replace gas-phase recirculation (which requires warming) with a magnetically coupled cryogenic liquid pump (e.g., Barber-Nichols BNCP series or custom gear pump)
- Keeps LAr in liquid phase during entire recirculation cycle — eliminates the purity degradation introduced by warm/cold cycling of the gas recirculation path
- Expected improvement: factor of 2–5 reduction in steady-state impurity level

**Resistive bulk impurity monitor array**
- Install 3–5 dedicated alpha-source purity monitors at different vertical heights in the cryostat
- Use 241Am 5.5 MeV alpha source in a sealed drift cell — provides continuous, local electron lifetime measurement with <1% statistical precision per minute
- Enables real-time spatial mapping of purity gradients → diagnose leak locations, inform fiducial volume cuts dynamically

---

## 5. Data Acquisition and Triggering

### Current Typical Baseline
Triggered DAQ based on PMT light signal, ~MHz ADC sampling, significant deadtime.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Continuous streaming readout with no hardware trigger**
- Implement a fully triggerless readout architecture: all channels digitized continuously at 2 MHz, data pushed to buffer nodes
- Use the FELIX (Front-End Link Exchange) board platform from ATLAS or a custom FPGA (Xilinx Ultrascale+ HBM) for online compression
- Lossless data compression (Huffman + zero-suppression) achieves ~10:1 reduction; achievable with existing FPGA resources
- Critical for supernova neutrino detection — a triggered system would miss the initial (and most physically interesting) low-energy burst

**Online reconstruction with GPU-accelerated wire-cell or graph neural network inference**
- Deploy NVIDIA A100/H100 GPUs in the DAQ backend running Wire-Cell or a GNN-based track finder in real time
- Enables online rejection of cosmic backgrounds (dominant background in surface prototypes) at >99% efficiency before data is written to tape
- Reduces data volume by ~100× → enables practical surface operation without a deep underground muon veto

**Precision timing distribution via White Rabbit protocol**
- Replace GPS-only timing with a White Rabbit (WR) network providing sub-ns synchronization across all DAQ nodes
- Critical for multi-module prototypes and for eventual synchronization with accelerator spill signals
- Specific hardware: WR switch v3.4, WR LEN (Low-End Node) cards on each readout crate

---

## 6. Cathode Design

### Current Typical Baseline
Solid stainless steel or FR4 cathode panel.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Transparent cathode (mesh or thin-strip design)**
- Replace solid cathode with a photon-transparent mesh (stainless 316L, 85% optical transmission) or thin-strip aluminum pattern
- Allows photon detectors to be placed behind the cathode plane or on the opposite drift volume wall with full solid-angle access
- Directly increases photon detection efficiency by 2× for detectors where cathode shadowing was previously dominant

**Resistive cathode coating for HV stability**
- Apply a 10–100 MΩ/□ resistive coating (diamond-like carbon or doped polyimide) to cathode surfaces
- Quenches microdischarge propagation — replaces a runaway Townsend discharge with a resistively-limited event
- Demonstrated in gaseous TPC work (RD51 collaboration); adaptation to LAr requires cryogenic resistivity characterization

---

## Summary Priority Matrix

| Upgrade | Physics Impact | Technical Readiness | Recommended Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pixel charge readout (LArPix) | Very High | TRL 4–5 | **1** |
| Cryogenic getter + liquid recirculation | Very High | TRL 7–8 | **2** |
| X-ARAPUCA + PEN reflector foils | High | TRL 5–6 | **3** |
| Continuous streaming DAQ | High | TRL 6–7 | **4** |
| Cold ASIC noise reduction | High | TRL 6 | **5** |
| Resistive field cage shell | Medium-High | TRL 5–6 | **6** |
| Transparent mesh cathode | Medium | TRL 6–7 | **7** |

---

## Critical Path Recommendation

The **two upgrades with largest combined impact for least development risk** are:

1. **Cryogenic inline getter + liquid-phase recirculation pump** — directly extends fiducial volume and improves energy resolution with well-understood technology
2. **X-ARAPUCA photon detector upgrade with PEN foils** — improves energy threshold and resolution for low-energy physics (solar neutrinos, supernova)

The pixel readout (LArPix) is the highest long-term physics impact item but carries the most integration risk for a near-term prototype iteration.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Kilometre-Scale Gravitational-Wave Interferometers

## Framing the Problem

Primary physics performance means **strain sensitivity** h(f) across the detection band (~1 Hz – 10 kHz), with sub-goals of:
- Lowering the noise floor (quantum, thermal, seismic, Newtonian)
- Extending the low-frequency reach
- Increasing the high-frequency sensitivity without sacrificing bandwidth

The fundamental noise budget has distinct dominant regions, so upgrades must be targeted accordingly.

---

## 1. Quantum Noise (Dominates across most of the band)

### 1a. Increased Circulating Power → Higher Input Laser Power

**Current state:** LIGO A+ circulates ~350 kW; input ~50 W after squeezing losses.

**Upgrade:**
- **Nd:YAG master-oscillator power-amplifier (MOPA) chains at 1064 nm scaled to 500 W**, using fiber amplifiers (Nufern/NKT large-mode-area Er:Yb co-doped fiber) followed by a bulk Nd:YAG end-stage to preserve beam quality (M² < 1.1).
- Higher power requires **parametric instability (PI) damping**: add **electrostatic drive rings** on test masses (already prototyped at Advanced LIGO) plus **acoustic mode dampers** — small lossy masses bonded to mirror barrel to dissipate acoustic resonances without adding thermal noise to the optical surface.
- **Thermal compensation upgrade:** replace CO₂ laser projectors with **spatially-programmable thermal actuators** (resistive wire arrays on compensation plates in the recycling cavities) to correct higher-order thermal lensing maps in real time.

### 1b. Frequency-Dependent Squeezing to 15+ dB

**Current state:** A+ uses ~15 dB injected squeezing (degraded to ~10 dB effective) with a 300 m filter cavity providing frequency rotation.

**Upgrade:**
- **Two cascaded filter cavities** (300 m + 16 m) to correct squeezing ellipse rotation with higher fidelity across the full band, reducing frequency-dependent loss mismatch.
- **Sub-threshold OPO squeezer with MgO:LiNbO₃ crystal** at 10 mm length, pumped at 532 nm, achieving >15 dB measured squeezing; replace current PPKTP crystals which show photodarkening at high pump powers.
- **Lossless Faraday isolators**: switch from bulk TGG Faraday rotators (absorption ~0.1%/cm at 1064 nm) to **crystalline iron garnet waveguide isolators** or, more practically, to **low-absorption TGG grown by Czochralski with post-annealing in O₂**, achieving <50 ppm/cm absorption.
- **Anti-reflection coated output mode-cleaner (OMC) with finesse >500** using ion-beam-sputtered (IBS) coatings to reduce round-trip loss below 100 ppm, preserving squeezing at readout.
- Long-term: **two-mode squeezing / variational readout** — replace homodyne detection with a **speed-meter topology** using a sloshing cavity (Khalili speed meter), which provides back-action evasion without the frequency-dependent squeezing infrastructure. Requires adding a ~150 m sloshing cavity in the output port.

### 1c. Signal Recycling Cavity Tuning for Broadband Response

- Replace fixed signal recycling mirror (SRM) with a **suspended, actuatable SRM** on a separate seismic platform allowing online detuning.
- Implement **optomechanical filter (white-light cavity)** using an anomalous-dispersion medium — specifically a **compound mirror cavity containing an atomic medium (Rb vapor cell)** or, more practically, an **active optomechanical element** (auxiliary cavity with a milligram-scale mirror driven to negative dispersion) to broaden the signal recycling bandwidth without losing peak sensitivity. This remains at TRL 4–5 but is the correct next step.

---

## 2. Mirror Thermal Noise (Dominant 10–200 Hz)

This is the hardest noise floor to push down and sets the sensitivity in the most astrophysically rich band.

### 2a. Test Mass Material Upgrade: Crystalline Silicon at Cryogenic Temperature

**The single highest-impact upgrade.**

- **Replace fused silica (FS) test masses** (mechanical loss angle φ ~10⁻⁷ at room temperature) with **mono-crystalline silicon (Si) cylinders**, 55 cm diameter × 55 cm, ~200 kg.
  - Si at 123 K has mechanical loss angle φ < 10⁻⁹ (two orders of magnitude better than FS at 300 K).
  - Si has zero coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) at 18 K and 123 K — thermal noise and thermoelastic noise both vanish at these temperatures.
  - Requires operating at **123 K** (second CTE zero, technically easier than 18 K).
  - Wafers for this size are not yet commercially available; requires **float-zone or Czochralski boule growth** at 55 cm diameter — currently the world's largest float-zone Si boules are ~20 cm, so **a dedicated crystal growth program** is necessary (e.g., partnering with Siltronic or Shin-Etsu at larger scale).

- **Cryogenic payload and marionette**: replace steel/FS suspension fibers with **silicon ribbon fibers** (30 μm × 1 mm cross-section, laser-cut from Si wafer) for the final suspension stage, to reduce suspension thermal noise and provide low thermal conductance to the cold mass. At 123 K, Si violin mode thermal noise is suppressed by a factor ~√(T·φ(T)) ≈ 30× relative to FS at 300 K.

- **Cryostat design**: each test mass housed in a **5-layer radiation shield cryostat** (outer vacuum, 77 K LN₂ shield, 4 K pulse-tube cooler shield, 123 K cold finger stage) with radiative cooling links — no conductive heat links to avoid vibration injection. Cooling power budget: ~1 W absorbed optical power at 1550 nm (see below) per mirror, extracted via thin Si or sapphire heat links to the penultimate suspension mass.

### 2b. Wavelength Change: 1550 nm

- Silicon is **opaque at 1064 nm** (bandgap 1.1 eV = 1127 nm). Cryogenic Si mirrors require switching to **1550 nm** telecom wavelength (Einstein Telescope baseline).
- **1550 nm laser source**: Er-doped fiber MOPA systems (e.g., NKT Photonics or IPG Photonics) can deliver 100–200 W at 1550 nm with excellent noise properties, directly compatible with Si test masses.
- All optics (beam splitter, recycling mirrors, mode cleaners) must be redesigned in **silicon or CaF₂** with IBS coatings optimized for 1550 nm.
- **Squeezed light at 1550 nm**: OPO using **PPLN (periodically poled lithium niobate)** waveguide squeezer, already demonstrated at >12 dB; highly mature at telecom wavelengths.

### 2c. Mirror Coating Upgrade (Critical Even With Si Substrates)

Brownian noise in the high-reflectivity coating currently limits sensitivity at ~100 Hz.

- **Replace Ta₂O₅/SiO₂ IBS coatings** with:
  - **Amorphous silicon (a-Si) / SiO₂ coatings**: a-Si has refractive index n ≈ 3.5 at 1550 nm vs. 2.1 for Ta₂O₅, meaning fewer layers needed, reducing coating thickness and noise by ~40%.
  - **Crystalline AlGaAs/GaAs coatings (epitaxial mirrors)**: grown by **molecular beam epitaxy (MBE)** on GaAs substrates, then substrate-removed and bonded to Si test masses via **direct wafer bonding**. Demonstrated mechanical loss angle φ ~10⁻⁵ — already better than Ta₂O₅ (φ ~2×10⁻⁴) and potentially improvable to 10⁻⁶ with annealing. Loss angle goal: φ < 5×10⁻⁶ at 123 K.
  - **Challenge**: coating uniformity over 55 cm aperture. Current AlGaAs bonded mirrors are ~15 cm. Requires development of **large-area MBE chambers** (possible but expensive; e.g., custom Veeco Lumina-scale systems).
  - Fallback near-term: **ion-beam-sputtered TiO₂:SiO₂ "titania-doped silica"** coatings with post-deposition annealing at 500°C (already in A+ mirrors), loss angle ~4×10⁻⁵ — factor 5 improvement over pure Ta₂O₅.

---

## 3. Seismic and Newtonian Noise (Below ~20 Hz)

### 3a. Active Seismic Isolation: Next-Generation Platforms

**Current state:** LIGO uses HAM/BSC platforms with 6-DOF active isolation achieving ~10⁻¹³ m/√Hz at 10 Hz.

**Upgrade:**
- **Inertial sensors**: replace current Sercel L-4C geophones with **cryogenic superconducting gravimeters (SGs)** or, more practically, **atom interferometer-based inertial sensors** achieving 10⁻¹⁰ g/√Hz at 1 Hz (e.g., Muquans/iXblue LP-10 cold-atom gravimeter). Use as low-noise error signals for the active platform servo below 1 Hz.
- **Horizontal isolation**: current HEPI actuators use voice coils. Replace with **Lorentz actuators on granite plinths with picometer-resolution capacitive sensors** (Physik Instrumente PI-Nano series) for the final positioning stage.
- **Six-axis AEI-SAS (Seismic Attenuation System)** from the AEI Hannover group: inverted pendulums for horizontal + geometric anti-spring (GAS) blades for vertical. Demonstrated 10× better isolation than HAM-SAS. Install at all test mass chambers.
- **Monolithic fused silica fiber suspensions** (already in Advanced LIGO) — maintain and extend to recycling cavity mirrors.

### 3b. Newtonian Noise Cancellation

Newtonian/gravity gradient noise (NN) sets a hard floor below ~20 Hz regardless of seismic isolation.

- **Deploy seismometer arrays**: 6–8 **Nanometrics Trillium Compact** broadband seismometers per test mass station, arranged in optimized 3D array geometry to reconstruct the local density fluctuation field.
  - Subtraction algorithm: **Wiener filter** estimated from seismic array + ML-based adaptive filter (LSTM network) for nonstationary noise.
  - Expected NN reduction: factor 10–100 depending on array size, achievable with current technology per Cella & Cuoco (2000) formalism.
- **Underground siting** (the most effective long-term solution): move to depths >100 m where seismic noise is reduced by 10×–100× at 1–10 Hz, reducing NN floor proportionally. This is the Einstein Telescope and NEMO approach. For an existing surface detector, this means the upgrade is **site relocation** — but excavating detector arms underground is the correct engineering path for 3rd-generation instruments.
- **Atmospheric NN**: install a **microphone array** (100 nodes) around the corner station to subtract infrasound pressure fluctuations driving gravity gradients.

- Improve the **penultimate mass (marionette) reaction chain**: use **magnetically levitated intermediate stages** (passive Halbach-array magnetic levitation in the < 1 Hz regime) to reduce mechanical cross-coupling.

## 5. Laser Frequency and Intensity Noise

### 5a. Pre-Stabilization and Reference Cavities

- **Ultra-stable reference cavity**: replace current 8 cm Zerodur spacer cavities with a **30 cm single-crystal silicon Fabry-Pérot cavity** at 124 K (where CTE = 0), suspended on a vibration-isolated platform. ### 5b. Intensity Noise

- **In-loop intensity stabilization photodetector**: replace single photodiode with a **balanced homodyne detector array** (4 × InGaAs photodiodes, quantum efficiency > 99%) to suppress classical intensity noise to shot noise at 10 Hz with 160 dB suppression bandwidth.

- **Digital control system**: migrate from current RCG (Real-time Code Generator on VME/PCIe) to a **low-latency optical fiber-linked FPGA system** (White Rabbit timing, <1 ns synchronization across km baselines), reducing control noise injection.
- **Parametric instability control**: real-time PI monitoring and damping using **electrostatic drive comb actuators** integrated into the test mass suspension cage, with frequency-selective ring damping matched to acoustic mode spectrum (finite element modeled for each test mass).

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Forward Flavour Physics Spectrometer

## Context and Performance Priorities

For a forward flavour spectrometer (think LHCb-topology: pseudorapidity ~2–5, high luminosity, heavy-flavour tagging, CP violation, rare decays), the primary physics performance drivers are:

- **Proper-time resolution** (drives CP asymmetry sensitivity)
- **Vertex resolution / impact parameter resolution** (b/c tagging, signal/background separation)
- **Momentum / mass resolution** (signal yield, background rejection)
- **Particle identification** (kaon/pion/proton separation for flavour tagging and final-state ID)
- **Trigger efficiency and rate capability** (especially at high luminosity)

---

## 1. Vertex Locator (VELO) — Impact Parameter & Decay-Time Resolution

### Current bottleneck
Material budget and pixel pitch limit IP resolution; RF foil proximity to beam limits closest approach.

### Proposed upgrades

**A. Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors (MAPS) at ~20 µm pitch**
- Replace hybrid pixels with MAPS (e.g., evolved from ALICE ITS3 / ARCADIA process) fabricated in 65 nm CMOS imaging technology
- Achieves spatial resolution ~3–4 µm per hit vs. ~12 µm current hybrid pixel
- Thinning to **50 µm** (epitaxial layer on substrate) reduces material to **~0.1% X₀ per layer** vs. ~0.5% X₀
- Enables IP resolution σ(IP) ∝ (p_T)⁻¹ to improve by factor ~2–3

**B. 4D tracking with integrated LGAD timing**
- Incorporate **AC-coupled LGAD (AC-LGAD)** layers with ~30 µm pitch achieving **30–50 ps** per-hit time resolution
- Adds a time coordinate to each vertex, dramatically reducing ghost tracks and pile-up confusion at high luminosity (e.g., 50+ visible pp interactions/crossing)
- Requires ~1 ns bunch crossing timing from bunch-crossing ID to anchor absolute time

**C. Closer beam approach with thin RF foil**
- Move inner radius from ~5 mm to **3 mm** from beam axis using thinner corrugated RF foil in **Be or advanced Al alloy**
- Combined with finer pitch, improves first-hit lever arm and thus IP resolution directly

---

## 2. Upstream / Downstream Tracker — Momentum Resolution

### Proposed upgrades

**A. Upstream tracker: µ-strip silicon at 50 µm pitch with time tagging**
- Replace scintillating fibre tracker with **silicon µ-strip layers (50 µm pitch, 300 µm thick)** in the low-occupancy forward region
- Intrinsic hit resolution ~10–15 µm improves track curvature measurement before the magnet
- Reduces material in acceptance

**B. Downstream tracker: Scintillating fibre + SiPM with improved SiPM**
- Upgrade SiPMs to **NUV-HD technology (FBK/Hamamatsu)** with lower dark count rate at room temperature (~100 kHz/mm²) and higher PDE (~55% at 420 nm)
- Reduce fibre diameter from 250 µm to **150 µm** with square cross-section packing for hit resolution improvement from ~75 µm → ~45 µm
- This directly improves mass resolution (σ_m/m) by ~20–30%

**C. Magnet upgrade**
- Replace warm dipole magnet with a **superconducting dipole** (NbTi or Nb₃Sn) increasing integrated field from ~4 Tm → **8–10 Tm**
- Directly halves momentum resolution σ(p)/p, crucial for B→µµ and B→hh mass peaks
- Cost/complexity is high but physics gain is large; SMOG2-style internal target compatibility must be preserved

---

## 3. RICH Detectors — Particle Identification

### Proposed upgrades

**A. RICH 1 (low-momentum PID, 1–60 GeV/c): Aerogel + C₄F₁₀ replaced by dual-radiator with granular photon detector**
- Replace current HPD photodetectors with **Silicon PhotoMultipliers (SiPMs, 1.3 mm × 1.3 mm pixels)** coupled to fused silica optics
- SiPMs achieve ~25% higher photon detection efficiency vs. HPDs, giving more Cherenkov photons per ring → better angular resolution per track
- Replace aerogel with **hydrophobic aerogel tiles, n=1.03** optimised for kaon/pion threshold separation at 2–10 GeV/c

**B. RICH 2 (high-momentum, 15–100 GeV/c): DIRC-bar technology**
- Replace gas radiator + spherical mirrors with **proximity-focusing DIRC** using fused silica bars (L~1 m) and a **MCP-PMT or SiPM expansion volume**
- Achieves Cherenkov angle resolution ~0.5 mrad/track vs. ~0.7 mrad current
- Radiation-hard: fused silica transparent to VUV, MCP-PMT with lifetime >10 C/cm²
- Reduces longitudinal depth by ~1 m, freeing space

**C. Time-of-Flight layer at ~10 m from IP**
- Insert a dedicated **AC-LGAD TOF wall** (σ_t ~20 ps per track) between RICH 1 and RICH 2
- Provides kaon/pion separation up to ~10 GeV/c independently, and proton/kaon to ~20 GeV/c
- Serves as cross-check and fills PID gaps when RICH rings are incomplete

---

## 4. Calorimeter System — Electron/Photon Performance

### Proposed upgrades

**A. ECAL: Sampling → crystal + SiPM**
- Replace Shashlik ECAL with **PWO-II crystals (as CMS ECAL)** or **LYSO crystals** read out by **SiPM arrays**
- Energy resolution improves from σ(E)/E ~ 10%/√E → **~3%/√E**
- Critical for B→K*γ, B_s→φγ, and dielectron modes
- SiPM readout handles the high-rate forward environment; requires careful temperature stabilisation (±0.1°C)

**B. Add a preshower / pre-converter layer**
- 2 X₀ **tungsten converter** + thin MAPS silicon layer in front of ECAL
- Provides e/γ separation and π⁰ rejection, improving electron ID purity by factor ~5

---

## 5. Muon System

**Replace wire chambers with µ-RPC or GEM + sTGC**
- In highest-rate inner region: replace MWPC with **triple-GEM detectors** (rate capability >10 MHz/cm² vs. ~1 kHz/cm² for MWPCs)
- In outer region: **resistive-plate chambers (RPC)** with improved timing (σ_t ~200 ps) for muon triggering
- Improves dimuon trigger purity directly impacting B→µµ reach

---

## 6. Trigger and DAQ — Enabling Real-Time Analysis

### Proposed upgrade: Full software trigger with AI-accelerated reconstruction

**A. FPGA + GPU heterogeneous farm**
- Deploy **AMD/Intel FPGAs** at L0 for raw data compression and fast cluster finding on detector frontend (Allen-style GPU trigger already partially implemented in LHCb Upgrade I)
- Scale to **10,000 GPU nodes (A100/H100 class)** for full real-time reconstruction at 30 MHz interaction rate
- Enables **inclusive b-hadron triggers** based on displaced vertices rather than single high-pT muons — recovers hadronic modes

**B. Graph Neural Network (GNN) track finding on FPGA**
- Implement **GNN-based hit association** on Xilinx Versal or Intel Stratix FPGA fabric
- Reduces fake track rate by ~factor 3 at high occupancy, crucial for maintaining vertex resolution under pile-up

---

## 7. Radiation Hardness Considerations

| Sub-detector | Dose region | Technology choice rationale |
|---|---|---|
| VELO MAPS | ~100 Mrad, 10¹⁶ n/cm² | 65 nm CMOS with radiation-hard layout rules |
| RICH SiPM | ~10 krad | Radiation-hard SiPM with p-on-n configuration |
| ECAL SiPM | ~1 Mrad inner | Radiation-hard SiPM, gain recovery protocols |
| GEM foils | ~100 krad | Standard Kapton GEM well-validated |

---

## Summary: Expected Physics Gains

| Upgrade | Key observable improved | Estimated gain |
|---|---|---|
| MAPS VELO (20 µm + LGAD) | σ(IP), σ(t) | ×2–3 improvement in proper-time resolution |
| Superconducting magnet + finer tracker | σ(m), σ(p)/p | ×2 mass resolution → factor ~4 in signal/background for narrow peaks |
| DIRC RICH + TOF | PID ε, mistag rate | ~30% improvement in tagging power ε_tag |
| Crystal ECAL | σ(E)/E for γ/e | ×3 energy resolution, ×5 e/γ purity |
| GPU/GNN trigger | Trigger efficiency | ×2–3 in hadronic mode yields |

The highest-impact single investment is the **MAPS-based VELO with integrated timing**, as vertex and IP resolution feed into essentially every flavour physics measurement. The second highest is the **superconducting magnet**, whose momentum resolution improvement benefits all exclusive decay mass fits.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Xenon Dark Matter Detectors

## Context and Performance Priorities

The primary physics performance metrics are: **lower energy threshold, reduced backgrounds, improved fiducial mass, and enhanced signal discrimination**. I'll address each systematically.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System (Highest Leverage Upgrade)

### Current Limitation
Conventional 3-inch Hamamatsu R11410 PMTs have ~35% quantum efficiency and introduce radioactive backgrounds (~1 mBq/PMT from uranium/thorium in borosilicate glass).

### Proposed Upgrades

**Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) as primary photosensors**
- Replace PMTs with tiled arrays of Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-Cryo or Hamamatsu VUV4 SiPMs
- Specific target: ~50% photon detection efficiency (PDE) at 175 nm (Xe scintillation wavelength) at ~170 K operating temperature
- Benefit: ~2× improvement in photoelectron yield → directly lowers energy threshold by improving statistical resolution at low energy
- Practical form factor: 6×6 mm² tiles arranged in close-packed arrays on PTFE-backed copper support rings
- Key engineering challenge: cryogenic capacitance management; use custom ASICs (e.g., CAEN FERS-5200 adapted for cryo) to handle high channel count

**Why this matters most**: S1 signal (primary scintillation) is the threshold-limiting factor. Going from ~10 detected photons/keV to ~20 photons/keV at sub-keV recoil energies dramatically extends sensitivity to solar neutrinos, sub-GeV dark matter, and low-mass WIMPs.

---

## 2. Photon Wavelength Shifting

### Current Limitation
Standard tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) coating on PTFE reflectors degrades over time, has inhomogeneous application, and absorbs rather than shifts some fraction of photons.

### Proposed Upgrade
**Evaporated p-terphenyl (pTP) thin-film coatings**
- Replace TPB with vacuum-evaporated pTP at controlled 200 nm thickness on all interior surfaces
- pTP offers superior UV transparency, more uniform deposition, and higher thermal stability at LXe temperatures
- Alternatively: **polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) structural panels** as self-shifting structural components, eliminating the separate coating step and reducing surface inhomogeneity
- Target: increase effective light yield from ~8 to >12 detected photons/keV for nuclear recoils

---

## 3. Field Cage and Electrode Design

### Current Limitation
Wire-based gate/anode electrodes create electroluminescence non-uniformities and generate spurious electron emission ("gate emission" backgrounds). Mesh electrodes introduce electron trapping.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Transparent conductive oxide (TCO) electrodes**
- Replace stainless steel wire grids with indium tin oxide (ITO) coated fused silica plates for gate and anode electrodes
- ITO on quartz: ~85% optical transmission at 175 nm, eliminates wire sag and vibration, dramatically reduces point-like electron emission sites
- Field uniformity improvement: from ±5% to <±1% across the active volume

**Electroformed copper field-shaping rings**
- Replace machined OFHC copper with electroformed ultra-pure copper rings (achievable U/Th < 0.01 ppb) for field cage
- Benefit: ~10× reduction in radioactive contribution from field cage hardware
- Vendor path: similar to electroforming used in MAJORANA Demonstrator

**Optimized drift field**
- Increase drift field from ~200 V/cm (LZ baseline) to 400–500 V/cm using higher-voltage feedthroughs
- Reduces electron attachment to electronegative impurities, improving charge collection efficiency and S2 resolution at low energies
- Requires: custom high-voltage ceramic feedthroughs rated to >100 kV at cryogenic temperatures (KYOCERA or custom alumina designs)

---

## 4. Xenon Purity and Recirculation

### Current Limitation
Electronegative impurities (O₂, H₂O, N₂) at ppt levels cause electron attachment, degrading S2 signals from deep in the detector.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Rare-gas purifier with increased flow rate**
- Deploy SAES MonoTorr PS4-MT50 or equivalent heated getter rated for 500 SLPM (vs. typical 50–100 SLPM in current experiments)
- Target: electron lifetime > 10 ms (vs. ~5 ms typical), enabling full-drift-length charge collection even in multi-tonne detectors
- Implement **redundant parallel getter loops** so one can be regenerated without interrupting detector operation

**Cryogenic distillation column for ⁸⁵Kr removal**
- Inline charcoal trap at 77 K followed by a packed distillation column
- Target: reduce ⁸⁵Kr to <0.01 ppt (g/g) — ⁸⁵Kr is a dominant ER background
- PandaX-4T demonstrated this approach; next-generation needs higher throughput columns with structured packing (Sulzer MellapakPlus)

**Online radon removal**
- Add a dedicated **radon trap**: activated charcoal column cooled to −40°C in a temperature-controlled enclosure, with bypass valves to allow trap regeneration
- Target: reduce ²²²Rn emanation contribution below 0.1 μBq/kg Xe

---

## 5. Veto Systems

### Current Limitation
Neutron and gamma backgrounds from detector components and cavern rock are incompletely vetoed.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer detector**
- Replace or augment pure water Cherenkov veto with 0.1% Gd-loaded linear alkylbenzene (LAB) scintillator
- Gd has neutron capture cross-section of ~49,000 barns; emits 8 MeV gamma cascade detectable with high efficiency
- Instrument with 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912 or equivalent PMTs at ~20% photocoverage
- Expected neutron veto efficiency improvement: from ~95% to >99% for single-scatter neutron backgrounds

**High-coverage inner veto**
- Surround the cryostat with a thin (5 cm) **borated polyethylene** layer thermalized neutron moderator before the liquid scintillator, reducing fast neutron flux

---

## 6. Data Acquisition and Trigger

### Current Limitation
High-channel-count systems with ~1 μs shaping times miss sub-keV S1 signals that consist of only 2–5 photons.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Waveform digitizers with reduced dead time**
- Replace CAEN V1724 (100 MHz, 14-bit) with **CAEN V1730** (500 MHz, 14-bit) or STRUCK SIS3316 (250 MHz, 16-bit) across all channels
- Zero-suppression with FPGA-level pulse finding to manage data rates

**Hardware-level coincidence trigger at 2-PMT threshold**
- Implement coincidence logic in FPGA fabric (Xilinx Ultrascale+) requiring only 2-photon coincidence within 100 ns for S1 trigger
- Current experiments typically require 3-fold coincidence; dropping to 2-fold extends threshold by ~30% in energy
- Requires improved dark count rate management (motivating SiPM temperature stabilization below 165 K)

**Machine learning-based online event classification**
- Deploy FPGA-based neural network inference (using hls4ml framework) for real-time pulse shape discrimination
- Enables hardware-level rejection of PMT afterpulsing and dark current at trigger level, reducing saved data rate while maintaining signal efficiency

---

## 7. Material Radiopurity

### Systemic Upgrade

**Underground electroformed copper for all structural components**
- All internal copper to be electroformed underground (as demonstrated at SURF) to avoid cosmogenic activation (⁶⁰Co)
- Target: <0.01 mBq/kg total gamma activity

**Low-radioactivity PTFE**
- Replace standard PTFE reflectors with **ultra-clean PTFE** produced from purified polytetrafluoroethylene feedstock (Chemours Teflon 7A processed to <1 ppt U/Th)
- PTFE is the dominant surface area material and a meaningful background contributor

**Acrylic removal**
- Eliminate acrylic vessel components (used in some designs for optical clarity) as acrylic has poor radiopurity control and ⁴⁰K contamination; replace with fused silica or PTFE structures

---

## Summary Priority Matrix

| Upgrade | Background Reduction | Threshold Improvement | Complexity | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement | Moderate | **High** | High | **1** |
| ITO electrodes | **High** | Moderate | Medium | **2** |
| Gd-LS veto | **High** | Low | Medium | **3** |
| 500 SLPM getter | Moderate | Moderate | Low | **4** |
| Electroformed Cu | Moderate | Low | Medium | **5** |
| 2-fold trigger | Low | **High** | Low | **6** |

---

## Most Impactful Single Upgrade

**SiPMs with optimized cryogenic readout ASICs** deliver the largest gain: doubling photon detection efficiency directly halves the energy threshold, which exponentially increases sensitivity to low-mass dark matter candidates and extends the detectable recoil energy spectrum downward into the sub-keV regime where spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross-section constraints are currently weakest.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for an Earlier-Generation Xenon Dark Matter Detector

## Context: Baseline Assumptions

Taking as reference a detector like XENON100 or LUX-era technology (~2010-2013): single-phase or dual-phase LXe TPC, ~100 kg fiducial mass, PMT-based readout, modest self-shielding, ~10 cm drift length.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System

### Primary Problem
Early PMTs (e.g., Hamamatsu R8778, R11410 precursors) had:
- **Quantum efficiency ~25-30%** for VUV (175 nm scintillation)
- **High intrinsic radioactivity** (~few mBq/PMT from U/Th in borosilicate glass)
- **Limited coverage** (~30-40% photocathode coverage)

### Specific Upgrades

**Replace PMTs with SiPMs (Silicon Photomultipliers)**
- Use **Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) VUV-HD SiPMs** or **Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPCs** with photon detection efficiency (PDE) ~24% at 175 nm without wavelength shifters, improvable to >35% with TPB-coated surfaces
- SiPMs have **~1000× lower radioactivity** per unit area vs. borosilicate PMTs
- Tile the entire TPC barrel and end-caps in SiPM arrays — achievable ~80%+ photocathode coverage vs. ~30%
- **Quantitative impact**: improving light yield from ~6-8 PE/keVee to ~15-20 PE/keVee dramatically improves energy threshold and nuclear recoil/electron recoil discrimination at low energy

**Wavelength Shifting Layer**
- Deposit **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) via vacuum evaporation** at ~0.2 mg/cm² on PTFE reflector panels and SiPM windows — converts 175 nm → 420 nm where SiPM PDE is ~50%
- Earlier detectors used inconsistent TPB coating; controlled deposition with **quartz crystal microbalance monitoring** ensures uniformity

---

## 2. Electric Field System

### Primary Problem
Early field cage designs produced:
- **Field non-uniformities** (>5-10%) causing position reconstruction errors and fiducial volume uncertainty
- **Electron-ion recombination losses** at low fields (~100-200 V/cm typical)
- **Electroluminescence gap instability** (anode-gate in dual-phase)

### Specific Upgrades

**Field Cage Redesign**
- Replace wire-wound resistor ladder with **ultra-low-radioactivity UHMWPE or PTFE field-shaping rings** with embedded copper strips, using **custom ultra-low-background resistors** (metal film, screened for U/Th <1 μBq/resistor)
- **Target field uniformity**: <0.5% variation across fiducial volume
- Implement **Greinacher/Cockcroft-Walton HV circuit** inside xenon vessel to avoid HV feedthrough failures

**Higher Drift Field**
- Upgrade HV system to sustain **500-1000 V/cm** (vs. ~100-300 V/cm in earlier detectors)
- This improves **electron lifetime** sensitivity and reduces recombination, sharpening S2 signal
- Use **corrugated PTFE insulators** to prevent surface discharge at higher voltage

**Anode/Gate Electrode**
- Replace single wire grid with **photolithographically etched stainless steel mesh** (50 μm wire, 1 mm pitch) for uniform electroluminescence gain
- Maintain **extraction field >10 kV/cm** at liquid surface for near-unity extraction efficiency (earlier designs: ~50-60% extraction)

---

## 3. Xenon Purification and Circulation

### Primary Problem
Electronegative impurities (O₂, H₂O) at ppb levels reduce electron lifetime, attenuating S2 for deep interactions — early systems achieved ~100-300 μs lifetime.

### Specific Upgrades

**High-Flow Getter System**
- Install **SAES MonoTorr PS4-MT50** or equivalent hot metal getter rated for **50-100 SLPM continuous flow**
- Coupled to a **cryogenic pump** (no oil contamination) — earlier systems often used oil-lubricated compressors introducing hydrocarbons
- Target: **electron lifetime >5 ms** (needed for full-volume fiducialization)

**Inline Purity Monitor**
- Add dedicated **small LXe purity monitor** (parallel drift cell with UV laser or alpha source) for **real-time continuous monitoring** rather than inferring from detector data
- Allows feedback control of purification rate

**Radon Removal**
- Install **cryogenic radon trap** (cold charcoal column at -100°C to -50°C) **inline in the gas circulation loop** — radon was a dominant background in early experiments
- Achieves **<0.1 mBq/kg ²²²Rn** vs. ~few mBq/kg in early detectors

---

## 4. Detector Vessel and Shielding

### Primary Problem
Early cryostats used standard-grade stainless steel and commercial titanium with U/Th at ~few mBq/kg, and insufficient self-shielding mass.

### Specific Upgrades

**Cryostat Material**
- Replace 316L stainless steel with **electroformed copper** (U/Th at <0.01 mBq/kg, vs. ~1 mBq/kg for steel) for inner vessel
- If copper is mechanically challenging, specify **"radio-pure" titanium** screened to <0.1 mBq/kg by ICP-MS before procurement (as used in later XENONnT/LUX-ZEPLIN designs)

**Outer Water Shield Enhancement**
- Upgrade from passive water tank to an **active Cherenkov muon veto** by adding **8" PMTs (e.g., R5912)** to existing water shield
- ~4π solid angle coverage, >99.5% muon tagging efficiency
- Eliminates cosmogenic neutron background that plagued earlier analyses

**Inner Xenon Self-Shielding**
- This is primarily a **mass scale** issue, but within fixed vessel: optimize **fiducial volume definition** using improved 3D position reconstruction (see Section 5) to push fiducial boundary closer to TPC walls — recovering 20-30% more fiducial mass

---

## 5. Data Acquisition and Position Reconstruction

### Primary Problem
Early DAQ systems (CAEN V1724 etc.) had:
- **14-bit, 100 MHz sampling** — marginal for resolving S1 photon arrival times
- **PMT-based position reconstruction** with ~1 cm r.m.s. resolution in z, ~2-3 cm in xy

### Specific Upgrades

**DAQ Upgrade**
- Deploy **250 MHz, 14-bit digitizers** (e.g., CAEN V1730) with **zero-suppression firmware**
- Implement **FPGA-based online pulse finding** to reduce data rate while preserving waveform for suspicious events
- Add **dedicated trigger processor** for sub-PE threshold triggers enabling S1 coincidence at 2-3 fold (vs. 4-fold in earlier systems) — directly lowers energy threshold

**Position Reconstruction Algorithm**
- Implement **neural network or Gaussian process** position reconstruction trained on **⁸³ᵐKr calibration data** — improves xy resolution from ~3 cm to <1 cm at low energies
- Better position reconstruction → tighter fiducial cut → lower background per unit exposure

---

## 6. Calibration Systems

### Primary Problem
Early detectors relied on external gamma sources and had limited low-energy nuclear recoil calibration.

### Specific Upgrades

**Internal Calibration Sources**
- Add **⁸³ᵐKr injection system** (via gas inlet with controlled valve) for spatially uniform energy calibration at 41.5 keV — maps detector response in 3D
- Install **tritiated methane (CH₃T) injection** capability for **electron recoil calibration at 0-18 keV** — directly calibrates the signal region
- Add **²⁴¹AmBe or ²⁵²Cf neutron source** on a **motor-driven external source deployment system** for nuclear recoil band calibration under identical field conditions

**DD Neutron Generator**
- Incorporate a compact **deuterium-deuterium (2.45 MeV) neutron generator** (e.g., Thermo Scientific MP320) on the outer shield — provides **mono-energetic neutrons** for precise nuclear recoil calibration and multiple-scatter rejection characterization

---

## Summary: Expected Performance Gains

| Parameter | Earlier Generation | With Upgrades | Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Light yield | ~6-8 PE/keVee | ~18-22 PE/keVee | ~3× |
| Electron lifetime | ~150-300 μs | >5 ms | ~20× |
| ²²²Rn background | ~few mBq/kg | <0.1 mBq/kg | ~30× |
| Energy threshold | ~5-8 keVnr | ~1-2 keVnr | ~4× |
| Electron recoil rejection | ~99.5% at 50% NR | ~99.9% at 50% NR | ~10× leakage reduction |
| Position resolution (xy) | ~3 cm | <1 cm | ~3× |

The **highest-leverage single upgrade** is the **SiPM photon detector replacement with TPB coating**, because improved light yield cascades into better discrimination, lower threshold, and improved position reconstruction simultaneously.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Germanium Detector Array for Rare Decays

## Context and Performance Priorities

For rare decay searches (neutrinoless double-beta decay, dark matter, rare nuclear processes), the primary physics performance metrics are:
- **Energy resolution** (signal/background separation)
- **Background rejection** (sensitivity scaling)
- **Detection efficiency** (exposure)
- **Energy threshold** (accessible phase space)

---

## 1. Detector Crystal Upgrades

### 1.1 Point-Contact Geometry (PPC) or Inverted-Coaxial Point-Contact (ICPC)

**Current limitation:** Coaxial detectors have large electrode capacitance → higher noise floor → worse threshold and resolution at low energy.

**Upgrade:**
- Implement **ICPC geometry** (as demonstrated in LEGEND-200): single small-area point contact (≤3 mm diameter boron-implanted n+ contact) on one face, large-area Li-drifted contact on the outside
- Capacitance reduced to **~1 pF** versus ~40 pF for coaxial
- Enables sub-keV thresholds and electronic noise contribution <0.5 keV FWHM

**Concrete spec:** Crystal diameter 75–105 mm, mass 1–2 kg, point contact diameter ≤3 mm, depletion voltage 2–4 kV

### 1.2 High-Purity Germanium with Reduced Net Impurity Gradient

- Crystal boules grown via **Czochralski method with active impurity control**: net carrier concentration <10⁹ cm⁻³, gradient <10⁷ cm⁻⁴ across the boule
- This reduces incomplete charge collection tails that smear the Q-value peak
- Source: ORTEC/Mirion or dedicated underground crystal growing facilities (eliminates cosmogenic activation during surface exposure)

### 1.3 Isotopically Enriched ⁷⁶Ge

- **Enrichment to >88% ⁷⁶Ge** (CENTRUS/Tenex cascade process)
- Direct sensitivity gain: signal rate ∝ isotopic abundance, backgrounds from ²⁰⁸Tl and others diluted per unit mass
- Underground reprocessing immediately after enrichment to minimize cosmogenic ⁶⁸Ge production (dominant internal background)

---

## 2. Front-End Electronics

### 2.1 Cryogenic ASIC Charge-Sensitive Preamplifiers

**Current limitation:** Room-temperature JFETs (e.g., 2SK152) have thermal noise ~15 eV RMS, and long cables from cold detector to warm preamp add capacitance.

**Upgrade:**
- Deploy **cryogenic SiGe BJT or CMOS ASICs** operating at 77–120 K mounted directly on the detector holder, <5 cm from the point contact
- Target: input noise current <10 fA/√Hz, input noise voltage <1 nV/√Hz
- Example technology: **IHP 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS process** (demonstrated to operate at 77 K, low 1/f noise corner ~10 kHz)
- Eliminates ~90% of cable capacitance contribution to noise

**Achievable improvement:** Energy resolution improvement from ~2.5 keV FWHM → <1.5 keV FWHM at Qββ = 2039 keV

### 2.2 Multi-Channel Digitizer with High Dynamic Range

- **16-bit, 250 MSample/s flash ADCs** (e.g., based on Struck SIS3316 or custom CAEN V1740 derivatives) with full waveform digitization
- Enables offline optimal filter (Gatti-Manfredi or cusp filter) shaping rather than hardware shaping — recovers ~15% energy resolution compared to hardware shaping
- Trigger-less DAQ with **ZLE (Zero-Length Encoding)** to reduce data volume while preserving sub-microsecond timing

### 2.3 Low-Noise HV Bias Supply

- Replace commercial HV modules with **ultra-stable, low-ripple custom bias supplies**: ripple <1 mV RMS at 3–5 kV, stability <10 ppm/°C
- Microphonic HV ripple broadens spectral lines; this is a frequently underestimated contribution

---

## 3. Pulse Shape Discrimination Hardware

### 3.1 Segmented or Pixelated Outer Contact

**Concept:** Divide the large-area Li-drifted contact into **6–18 azimuthal/axial segments** using laser scribing

- Each segment read out independently with dedicated low-noise preamp channel
- Enables **2D event localization** within crystal: single-site events (SSE, signal-like) versus multi-site events (MSE, background-like γ interactions) separated with >95% efficiency
- Demonstrated in GERDA Phase II segmented detectors; needs scaling to ICPC geometry

**Concrete implementation:** 6-fold azimuthal segmentation + 2 axial rings = 12 channels per crystal; segmentation gap width 0.5–1 mm achieved by laser ablation

### 3.2 Current Pulse Shape Analysis via High-Bandwidth Preamp

- Bandwidth extension to **50–100 MHz** (versus typical 10 MHz) in the charge-sensitive preamp feedback network (reduce feedback capacitor to 0.1 pF, feedback resistor 500 MΩ → 50 MΩ with pole-zero cancellation in digital domain)
- Preserves fast current pulse shape information: rise time differences between SSE and MSE events are 50–200 ns — only resolvable with ≥100 MHz bandwidth
- Directly improves A/MSE separation from ~90% → >99% at signal efficiency >90%

---

## 4. Active Veto and Background Suppression

### 4.1 Liquid Argon (LAr) Veto Instrumentation Upgrade

**Current best practice (GERDA/LEGEND):** WLS-fiber + SiPM readout of LAr scintillation

**Upgrade specifics:**
- Replace WLS fibers with **direct-immersion VUV-sensitive SiPMs** (Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPC or FBK VUV-HD3, peak sensitivity at 128 nm Ar scintillation)
- Achieve **4π solid angle coverage >80%** using tetrahedral SiPM tile arrangement on inner cryostat wall
- Tile density: ~1 SiPM per 25 cm², total ~500 devices for a 1-m diameter active volume
- LAr veto efficiency for ²⁰⁸Tl events: improve from ~80% → >95%

### 4.2 Nitrogen-Flushed Dead-Layer Minimization

- Reduce outer dead-layer thickness via **Li implantation optimization**: target dead-layer <0.5 mm (versus typical 0.7–1.0 mm on n-type outer contact)
- Thin dead layer increases efficiency for low-energy events and reduces internal self-shielding uncertainty

### 4.3 Muon Veto Upgrade

- Plastic scintillator panels replaced with **water Cherenkov volume + 8" PMTs (R5912)** or large-area SiPMs
- Water Cherenkov provides: muon detection efficiency >99.9%, serves as additional neutron moderator, easier to scale to larger underground halls
- Include **gadolinium-loaded water (0.1% GdSO₄)** to capture and detect spallation neutrons (Gd thermal capture cross-section 49,000 barn, produces 8 MeV γ cascade detectable in PMTs)

---

## 5. Mechanical and Thermal Design

### 5.1 Low-Mass, Low-Radioactivity Detector Holders

**Current limitation:** PTFE/copper holders contribute U/Th contamination near detectors

**Upgrade:**
- Machine holders from **electroformed copper** (OFHC electroformed underground, <0.1 μBq/kg ²²⁶Ra)
- Replace PTFE contact springs with **silicon monolithic flexures** (photo-etched, assayed to <1 μBq/kg)
- Target holder mass: <50 g per detector (versus ~150 g typical), reducing gamma background from holder by 3×

### 5.2 Cryostat Material Upgrade

- Replace stainless steel inner cryostat with **electroformed copper or titanium** (Ti has lower intrinsic radioactivity than SS)
- Inner surface electropolished and cleaned to <10 μBq/kg ²²⁶Ra
- Use **indium-sealed flanges** rather than o-rings (eliminate outgassing hydrocarbons that can deposit on detector surfaces)

### 5.3 Active Temperature Stabilization

- Temperature fluctuations → leakage current variations → baseline noise
- Install **PID-controlled heater resistors + calibrated Cernox thermometers** at each detector string, stabilize to ±5 mK
- Reduces gain drift to <0.01 keV/hour, enabling longer physics runs between calibrations

---

## 6. Calibration System

### 6.1 Deployable Multi-Source Calibration

- **²²⁸Th wire sources** deployable on motorized systems into the LAr volume (2615 keV line close to Qββ)
- Add **⁸³ᵐKr gas injection** system for low-energy calibration (9.4 keV, 32.1 keV lines) — critical for threshold characterization
- Both enable **in-situ energy scale drift monitoring** without opening the cryostat

### 6.2 LED/Laser Charge Injection

- Fiber-coupled **UV LED pulser** (265 nm, <1 ns pulses) to each detector for electronic gain monitoring between source deployments
- Stabilizes gain to <5 ppm between calibration runs

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Germanium Detector Array for Rare Decays

## Context and Performance Drivers

For rare decay searches (neutrinoless double-beta decay, dark matter, rare nuclear transitions), the primary physics figures of merit are:
- **Energy resolution** at the signal region
- **Background index** (counts/keV/kg/yr)
- **Detection threshold**
- **Active mass / duty cycle**

---

## 1. Detector Crystal Upgrades

### 1.1 Point-Contact Geometry (PPC) or Inverted-Coaxial Point-Contact (ICPC)

**Current limitation:** Conventional coaxial detectors have large electrode areas, high capacitance (~30–50 pF), and poor low-energy performance.

**Upgrade:**
- Deploy **Inverted Coaxial Point Contact (ICPC)** crystals — single-crystal germanium with a small-area (~3 mm diameter) lithium-diffused point contact and a boron-implanted surface contact
- Achieves capacitance **< 1 pF**, directly reducing electronic noise floor
- Enables **sub-keV thresholds** (achievable ~100–200 eV) critical for dark matter and low-energy rare decays
- ICPC geometry simultaneously provides **large mass per crystal** (~2 kg) with good pulse-shape discrimination

**Concrete specification:** ICPC detectors fabricated from zone-refined, ultra-pure Ge (impurity concentration < 10¹⁰ cm⁻³), with crystal mass 1.5–2.5 kg, deployed in LEGEND-style string configurations.

### 1.2 Isotopically Enriched Material

- For ⁰νββ targets: enrich to **≥ 92% ⁷⁶Ge** (current state-of-art is ~88%)
- Enrichment via centrifuge cascades; the marginal physics gain per additional % enrichment in a background-limited regime is direct signal enhancement
- Evaluate **⁸²Se-doped** or alternative isotopes depending on Q-value accessibility

### 1.3 Surface Passivation Layer Optimization

- Replace conventional amorphous germanium (a-Ge) surface layers with **hydrogen-passivated surfaces** or optimized a-Ge thickness (< 50 nm)
- Reduces incomplete charge collection in the near-surface dead layer
- Critical for background rejection from alpha/beta surface events — thinner dead layer improves both efficiency and surface event identification

---

## 2. Front-End Electronics

### 2.1 Charge-Sensitive Amplifier (CSA) Redesign

**Current bottleneck:** Electronic noise (ENC) at the CSA input dominates energy resolution for point-contact detectors.

**Upgrade — Cryogenic JFET or HEMT preamplifiers:**
- Replace room-temperature JFET front-ends with **cryogenic silicon JFETs** operated at 100–130 K (sweet spot for Si JFET noise)
- Target: **ENC < 20 electrons RMS** (compared to ~50–100 e⁻ for warm front-ends)
- Alternatively, deploy **GaAs or InP HEMTs** cooled to 4 K for even lower noise figures; demonstrated ENC ~ 5–10 e⁻ RMS at mK temperatures in prototype systems

**Concrete component:** Toshiba 2SK369 or Linear Integrated Systems LSK389 JFETs operated cryogenically, or custom InP HEMT ASICs (similar to ATLAS/CMS tracker front-ends adapted for low capacitance).

### 2.2 Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) Digitization

- Deploy **ASIC-based digitizers** (e.g., SIS3316 FADC equivalent functionality in custom ASIC, or adapted from nEXO's SLAC ASIC)
- 14–16 bit ADC resolution at 250 MHz sampling rate per channel
- Integrate **Pole-Zero Cancellation** and **Trapezoidal Filter** shaping in firmware (FPGA-based DSP)
- Reduces cable count and thermal load inside the cryostat — critical for scaling to tonne-scale

### 2.3 On-Detector Signal Multiplexing

- Implement **time-division or frequency-division multiplexing** (TDM/FDM) to reduce number of feedthrough lines
- Leverage **SQUID-based multiplexing** if moving to mK operation (see Section 5)
- Each feedthrough penetration is a potential background source and thermal load

---

## 3. Shielding and Passive Background Reduction

### 3.1 Ultra-Low Background Inner Shield

**Replace conventional lead/copper shields with:**

- **Electroformed copper** (OFHC-grade, underground-electroformed to minimize cosmogenic ⁶⁰Co activation): inner shield layer 10–15 cm thick, activity < 0.3 μBq/kg in ²²⁶Ra
- This is already best practice; the upgrade is **increasing the thickness uniformity** and eliminating all mechanical fasteners by using precision-machined interlocking pieces without hardware

- **Argon or nitrogen gas purge** between copper shield and outer lead to eliminate ²²²Rn daughters plating onto surfaces

### 3.2 Active Liquid Argon (LAr) Veto

**High-impact upgrade for background suppression:**
- Immerse detector array in **instrumented liquid argon** acting simultaneously as coolant and active veto
- LAr scintillates at 128 nm; instrument with:
  - **Wavelength-shifting (WLS) fiber curtains** (e.g., TPB-coated fibers, Saint-Gobain BCF-91A) coupled to **SiPMs** (Hamamatsu VUV4 or FBK VUV-HD at 87 K)
  - Alternatively, **PTFE-reflector-lined LAr volume** with SiPM tile arrays on end-caps
- Target: **> 99.9% veto efficiency** for multi-site Compton scattering backgrounds
- Demonstrated in GERDA Phase II / LEGEND-200: background index improvement factor ~10× over unvetoed operation

**Concrete SiPM specification:** FBK VUV-HD3 (3 mm × 3 mm cells, 35 μm microcell pitch), operated at ~150 V bias, achieving PDE > 20% at 128 nm at 87 K.

### 3.3 Radon Mitigation Infrastructure

- **Radon-tight glove box** for all detector handling with continuous radon monitoring (< 1 mBq/m³)
- **Radon-free nitrogen blanket** inside all cryostat volumes during assembly
- **Activated charcoal radon traps** on all gas inlets, with trap efficiency > 99.99%
- Dedicated **radon emanation measurement** of all components before installation (minimum detectable activity ~ 1 μBq)

---

## 4. Pulse Shape Discrimination (PSD) Enhancement

### 4.1 Multi-Site Event Rejection via Waveform Analysis

**Upgrade — High-bandwidth digitization:**
- Increase digitizer bandwidth from ~10 MHz to **250 MHz** sampling with 14-bit resolution
- Enables resolution of **charge collection timing** at sub-100 ns level
- Implement **A/E parameter** (current amplitude / energy) discrimination in FPGA firmware for real-time background flagging
- Current best: ~90% background rejection at 90% signal efficiency; target >95% signal efficiency at same background suppression

### 4.2 Segmented Read-Out for Position Sensitivity

- Deploy **2D or 3D segmented germanium** detectors with **6-fold azimuthal segmentation** and **2-fold longitudinal segmentation** per crystal
- Provides **position reconstruction to ~5 mm** — suppresses surface backgrounds and improves multi-site discrimination
- Trade-off: increased channel count and complexity; appropriate for crystals not amenable to point-contact geometry

### 4.3 Machine Learning PSD

- Implement **convolutional neural network (CNN) pulse-shape classifier** trained on calibration data (Th-228 source)
- Run inference on dedicated **FPGA co-processor** (Xilinx Ultrascale+) at trigger level
- Expected improvement: **15–25% additional background rejection** over cut-based A/E method, as demonstrated in simulation studies (GERDA/LEGEND analyses)

---

## 5. Cryogenic and Mechanical Infrastructure

### 5.1 Bolometric Phonon Readout (Hybrid Mode)

**Next-generation upgrade — operate as cryogenic bolometers:**
- Cool germanium detectors to **~10–20 mK** using a dilution refrigerator (wet or dry)
- Attach **Neutron Transmutation Doped (NTD) Ge thermistors** or **Transition Edge Sensors (TES)** to read out both phonon and ionization signals simultaneously
- **Dual ionization+phonon readout** (as in CDMSiiGe / SuperCDMS Ge HV detectors):
  - Phonon channel: bolometric resolution ~1 keV FWHM on bulk signal
  - Ionization channel: standard charge collection
  - **Discrimination of nuclear recoil vs. electron recoil** at > 99.9% efficiency using ionization yield
- Enables simultaneous rare decay and WIMP dark matter physics from same hardware

**Concrete component:** NTD-Ge thermistors fabricated at ILL Grenoble, resistance ~1 MΩ at 20 mK, heat capacity matched to crystal mass; or **NIST TES** (Mo/Cu bilayer, Tc ~80 mK).

### 5.2 Vibration Isolation and Microphonics Suppression

- **Spring-loaded suspension** for detector strings with resonance frequency < 1 Hz
- **Stainless steel bellows** at all cryostat penetrations to decouple mechanical vibrations from cooling lines
- **Active vibration cancellation** (piezo-actuators in feedback loop) at cryostat mounting points
- Critical because microphonics generates low-frequency noise that limits threshold and PSD quality

### 5.3 Low-Radioactivity Cryogenic Hardware

- Replace all conventional stainless steel hardware inside shield with **radio-assayed electroformed copper or PTFE** fasteners
- Specifically: eliminate **all standard commercial screws** (typically ~10 mBq/kg in ²²⁶Ra) in favor of custom-made components with radioactivity measured at < 0.1 mBq/kg
- Use **ultrasonic bonding** of wire connections rather than solder (solder flux residues emanate radon)

---

## 6. Calibration System

### 6.1 Deployable Source System with Reduced Activation

- Replace wire-deployed ²²⁸Th calibration sources (which require opening the cryostat) with **permanently installed but retractable** source tubes: thin-walled PTFE tubes routed between detector strings
- Sources retracted to **outside active volume** during physics runs — eliminates background contribution during data-taking while maintaining rapid calibration deployment (< 30 min)

### 6.2 In-Situ Energy Scale Monitoring

- Instrument with **⃰⁸³ᵐKr injection system**: krypton-83m (T₁/₂ = 1.86 h) dissolved in LAr provides continuous 41.5 keV calibration lines
- Alternatively, **⁵⁷Co or ²⁴¹Am γ sources** in fixed geometry outside the active shield for continuous gain monitoring
- Enables **sub-0.1 keV energy scale stability** tracking — critical near Q-value of ⁷⁶Ge (2039 keV)

---

## 7. Data Acquisition and Trigger

### 7.1 Triggerless / Continuous Digitization

- Move from hardware-threshold-triggered DAQ to **continuous waveform streaming** at 25 kHz effective bandwidth per channel
- Store **all data** and apply software triggers in offline analysis
- Eliminates trigger dead-time and enables retrospective threshold-lowering as analysis methods improve
- Requires ~**50 TB/year per 100 channels** of storage — addressable with modern commodity storage arrays

### 7.2 Real-Time Coincidence Rejection

- Implement **hardware coincidence logic** in FPGA: veto any germanium event within **±10 μs** of a LAr scintillation signal exceeding threshold
- Real-time muon veto: coincidence with external muon plastic scintillator panels within **±100 μs** window
- Reduces online data rate by factor ~3–5, easing DAQ requirements

---

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Germanium Detector Array for Rare Decays

## Context and Performance Priorities

For rare decay searches (neutrinoless double-beta decay, dark matter, rare nuclear transitions), primary physics performance means:
- **Energy resolution** (signal/background separation)
- **Background rejection** (sensitivity scales with signal/√background)
- **Detection efficiency and livetime**
- **Energy threshold** (for low-Q-value decays or sub-keV signals)

---

## 1. Detector Crystal Upgrades

### 1.1 Enriched, Zone-Refined Crystals with Reduced Dislocation Density
**Specific upgrade:** Move from standard Czochralski-grown Ge to zone-refined crystals with dislocation density <100 cm⁻² (versus typical 500–2000 cm⁻²).

- **Why it matters:** Dislocations trap charge carriers, causing incomplete charge collection and low-energy tails on photopeaks — directly degrading energy resolution from ~2.0 keV FWHM at 2 MeV toward the theoretical limit (~1.3 keV FWHM at 2 MeV for 2νββ/0νββ searches)
- **Concrete technology:** Use the ORTEC/Mirion ultra-low-dislocation growth process; request EPD (Etch Pit Density) certification per boule
- **Enrichment:** For ⁷⁶Ge experiments, >87% ²⁶Ge enrichment from Russian URENCO-type centrifuge cascade + subsequent reprocessing with electrolytic Ge reduction before crystal growth

### 1.2 Inverted-Coaxial Point Contact (ICPC) Geometry
**Specific upgrade:** Replace true-coaxial or BEGe detectors with ICPC detectors at ~1–2 kg per crystal.

- **Why:** ICPCs combine the large mass of coaxial detectors with the single-charge-collection-point topology of point contacts
- **Benefit:** Weighting potential concentrated at point contact → drift-time-based pulse shape discrimination (PSD) with figure-of-merit comparable to BEGe but at 4–8× the mass per unit
- **Concrete spec:** 85 mm diameter × 80 mm length, p-type ICPC with lithium-diffused outer contact <1 mm dead layer; boron-implanted point contact <0.3 μm
- **Demonstrated by:** LEGEND-200 deployment at Gran Sasso (MJD and GERDA heritage)

### 1.3 Thinned Dead Layer on p-type Contact
**Specific upgrade:** Transition outer n+ lithium-diffused contact to implanted contacts or amorphous germanium (a-Ge) contacts.

- **Current problem:** Li-diffused n+ contacts are ~0.5–1 mm thick → dead layer degrades low-energy response and creates surface background
- **Upgrade:** Hydrogenated amorphous germanium (a-Ge) passivation layers at 50–200 nm thickness (developed by LBNL/SURF groups)
- **Physics impact:** Lowers effective energy threshold from ~200 keV to <5 keV; critical for light dark matter and solar neutrino searches

---

## 2. Front-End Electronics

### 2.1 Cryogenic ASIC Charge-Sensitive Preamplifiers
**Specific upgrade:** Replace room-temperature FET-based preamplifiers with cryogenic ASICs operating at 77–120 K directly at the detector.

- **Concrete technology:** 
  - **SiGe BJT ASICs** (e.g., IHP SG13G2 0.13 μm BiCMOS process) — demonstrated noise of 20–30 e⁻ ENC at 100 K
  - Alternatively: **GaAs MESFET** front-end (heritage from CDEX/PandaX-III)
  - Target: **FWHM contribution from electronics noise <0.1 keV** at 2 MeV, versus ~0.3–0.5 keV for room-temperature chain
- **Specific design:** Integrate the JFET/SiGe first stage within 5 cm of detector in vacuum cryostat; use Kapton flex PCB with 10 μm traces to minimize capacitance to <1 pF (detector capacitance ~1–2 pF for point contacts)
- **Why critical:** Johnson noise from feedback resistor (typically 1–10 GΩ) dominates at low frequency; replace resistor feedback with **pulsed-reset transimpedance amplifier** (PRTA) to eliminate this noise floor entirely

### 2.2 Pulsed-Reset Preamplifier Architecture
**Specific upgrade:** Replace resistive-feedback CSPs with inhibited pulsed optical reset or electronic reset designs.

- **Eliminates:** 1/f noise contribution from feedback resistor (~10–50 eV FWHM contribution)
- **Technology:** Use an LED reset or charge injection reset triggered when integrator approaches saturation; implemented in LEGEND with custom LMFE (Low-Mass Front-End) boards
- **Spec target:** Input referred noise <10 e⁻ rms ENC at full 1 kg detector capacitance

### 2.3 High-Resolution Digitizers
**Specific upgrade:** Replace shaping amplifier + ADC chains with direct **Flash ADC waveform digitizers** at 250 MHz, 16-bit resolution.

- **Concrete products/specs:** 
  - Struck SIS3316 (250 MHz, 14-bit) → upgrade to custom 250 MHz, 16-bit pipeline ADC (AD9467 or equivalent)
  - Or: Caen V1724 (100 MHz, 14-bit) → Caen V1730 (500 MHz, 14-bit) for better leading-edge timing
- **Physics benefit:** Full waveform capture enables offline optimization of trapezoidal filter parameters, multi-site event rejection via A/E (current amplitude over energy) analysis, and machine-learning-based PSD — all software-defined without hardware changes

---

## 3. Pulse Shape Discrimination Hardware

### 3.1 Segmented or Orthogonal-Strip Electrode Geometry
**Specific upgrade:** For detectors >500 g, implement 6-fold or 18-fold segmentation of the outer lithium contact.

- **Technology:** Laser scribing of the Li-diffused contact into segments, each read by independent preamplifier channel
- **Physics benefit:** Localizes energy deposition in 3D → multi-site event (MSE) rejection efficiency >99% for Compton scatter background at Qββ
- **Concrete example:** AGATA/MINIBALL-style 36-fold segmented HPGe; for 0νββ the simpler 6-fold segmentation (GERDA Phase-I heritage) provides factor ~3 background reduction with manageable channel count

### 3.2 Point-Contact Topology with A/E PSD
Even without segmentation, **maximize A/E discrimination** by:
- Minimizing point-contact area to <3 mm diameter (reduces capacitance, sharpens weighting potential)
- Using sub-ns rise-time digitization to resolve current pulse shape
- **Demonstrated rejection:** MSE suppression factor >200 at 90% DEP efficiency (GERDA/LEGEND numbers)

---

## 4. Cryogenic Infrastructure

### 4.1 Liquid Argon Active Veto Instrumentation
**Specific upgrade:** Instrument the liquid argon (LAr) surrounding the Ge array as an active veto scintillator.

- **Concrete technology:** 
  - **SiPM-based light detection:** Hamamatsu VUV4 (S13370 series, 6 mm²) or FBK VUV-HD3 tiles optimized for 128 nm LAr scintillation wavelength
  - Coverage: >3 sr solid angle with SiPM tiles on copper/PTFE reflector shroud
  - Wavelength shifter: **Tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB)** evaporated at 0.2 mg/cm² on VM2000 reflector foil
  - Alternatively: **PMMA fiber curtain** (Saint-Gobain BCF-91A WLS fibers) for 4π coverage with fewer readout channels
- **Physics impact:** LAr veto achieves ~90% rejection of Compton-scatter backgrounds; this is the single largest background reducer after PSD
- **Target performance:** >99.9% veto efficiency for events depositing >100 keV in LAr simultaneously with Ge signal

### 4.2 Low-Vibration Pulse-Tube Cryocoolers
**Specific upgrade:** Replace liquid nitrogen/liquid helium bath cooling with **PT415 or PT420 Cryomech pulse-tube refrigerators** with active vibration compensation.

- **Problem:** Mechanical vibrations from PTRs induce microphonic noise in Ge detectors (capacitance modulation of detector/cable → excess noise)
- **Solution:** 
  - Use **remotely-located compressor** (5–10 m flex line) to isolate vibration source
  - Add **piezoelectric active damping stage** (e.g., Minus K or custom) between cold head and detector plate
  - Alternatively: **3He/4He dilution refrigerator** for mK-range operation (enables bolometric mode — see below)
- **Quantified benefit:** Reduce microphonic noise contribution from ~50 eV to <5 eV FWHM

---

## 5. Background Reduction Hardware

### 5.1 Ultra-Low-Background Electroformed Copper Structural Components
**Specific upgrade:** Replace all structural copper near detectors with **underground electroformed copper** (UEFCU).

- **Specific source:** SURF underground electroforming facility (heritage: MAJORANA DEMONSTRATOR) produces Cu with ²³²Th <0.1 μBq/kg and ²³⁸U <0.1 μBq/kg — ~1000× cleaner than OFHC commercial copper
- **Components to upgrade:** Detector mounting strings, string support structure, inner cryostat vessel, cable conduits
- **Why critical:** ²⁰⁸Tl (2615 keV γ from ²³²Th chain) is the dominant external background at Qββ(⁷⁶Ge) = 2039 keV; reducing structural material radioactivity directly reduces ROI background index

### 5.2 Radon Exclusion System
**Specific upgrade:** Implement a **closed-loop boil-off nitrogen purge** with real-time ²²²Rn monitor.

- **Technology:** 
  - Electrostatic Rn monitor (Durridge RAD7 or custom electrostatic collector) at sensitivity <1 mBq/m³
  - Activated charcoal Rn trap (6 kg charcoal at −40°C) on N₂ supply line
  - Glove-box purge system maintaining <0.1 Bq/m³ Rn during detector installation
- **Physics impact:** ²²²Rn → ²¹⁰Pb plate-out on detector surfaces is a leading surface background source; reducing by ×100 directly improves sensitivity

### 5.3 Muon Veto Upgrade
**Specific upgrade:** Replace plastic scintillator panels with **water Cherenkov veto + gadolinium doping**.

- **Technology:**
