- Reference implementation path: DARWIN/XLZD conceptual design already targets this

**Wavelength-shifting reflector enhancement**
- Replace current PTFE reflectors with **TPB (tetraphenyl butadiene) vacuum-evaporated coatings at 1–2 mg/cm²** on all inner surfaces
- Shift 175 nm → 420 nm where SiPM efficiency peaks
- Achievable reflectance: >95% vs. ~93% bare PTFE at VUV

---

## 2. TPC Field Cage and Electrode Design

### Current Limitation
Wire grids (gate, anode, cathode) made of stainless steel or Be-Cu introduce radioactive contamination and cause electron attachment/field distortions.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Photolithographically patterned mesh electrodes**
- Use **electroformed copper meshes on PTFE frames** (100–200 µm pitch, >95% optical transparency) instead of tensioned wires
- Copper electroforming achieves <1 ppb U/Th vs. ~ppm in bulk stainless steel
- More uniform electric field → better fiducialization and position reconstruction

**Resistive field cage strips**
- Replace discrete copper rings with **evaporated ITO (Indium Tin Oxide) resistive strips on fused silica or PTFE cylinders**
- ITO resistivity tunable to eliminate field distortions from charge accumulation on PTFE
- Achieves <0.1% field uniformity vs. ~1–2% with copper rings

**Higher drift field capability**
- Upgrade HV feedthroughs to sustain **1000 V/cm** (vs. typical 200–500 V/cm)
- Use **PTFE-insulated coaxial HV cables with custom ceramic feedthroughs** (alumina or sapphire) baked at >400°C to outgas radon precursors
- Higher field reduces electron diffusion, improving spatial resolution and fiducial boundary sharpness

---

## 3. Xenon Purification and Radon Removal

### Current Limitation
Radon (²²²Rn, ²²⁰Rn) emanating from detector surfaces and plumbing creates beta/alpha backgrounds near the WIMP search region of interest. This is currently the **dominant surface background** in LZ and XENONnT.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Radon-trapping cold trap upgrade**
- Dedicated **activated charcoal trap at 190–200 K** with >10⁴ radon reduction factor in the gas recirculation loop
- Use **coconut-shell activated carbon (Saratech or equivalent)** baked at 200°C under vacuum to reduce emanation from the trap itself
- Flow rate: maintain full xenon inventory recirculation in <24 hours
- Achieve target: <1 µBq/kg ²²²Rn in liquid xenon (XENONnT demonstrated ~4 µBq/kg; target 10× lower)

**Electropolished low-emanation stainless steel**
- All gas-contact surfaces: **316L SS electropolished + passivated**, tested to <1 µBq/m² radon emanation
- Replace all elastomer O-rings with **metal C-ring seals (Helicoflex type)** — elastomers are major radon sources

**Online distillation column**
- Cryogenic distillation to remove **Kr (⁸⁵Kr background) and Rn in real-time** during operation
- Target: ⁸⁵Kr < 0.01 ppt (mol/mol) — approximately 100× below current LZ levels
- Use structured packing columns (Sulzer MellapakPlus) with reflux condensers integral to the xenon handling system

---

## 4. Outer Detector and Veto Systems

### Current Limitation
Neutron and gamma backgrounds from detector materials and cavern rock penetrate the active volume. Current gadolinium-doped water Cherenkov vetoes have ~95% neutron capture efficiency but leave gaps.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator (Gd-LS) outer detector**
- Replace water Cherenkov with **0.1% Gd-loaded LAB (linear alkylbenzene) + PPO scintillator** at 20–40 tonnes surrounding the cryostat
- Gd captures thermal neutrons with ~8 MeV gamma cascade, detectable with ~>99.9% efficiency
- Light yield ~8000 photons/MeV vs. ~300 Cherenkov photons/MeV in water → much lower threshold
- Readout: 8-inch PMTs (Hamamatsu R5912 or equivalent) at ~20% coverage
- Demonstrated by PROSPECT and SNO+ at smaller scale

**Active muon veto integration**
- **Plastic scintillator panels** (EJ-200 or equivalent, 5 cm thick) tiling the outer water tank inner surface
- Time-of-flight tagging of cosmogenic neutrons produced by muon spallation up to **1 µs after muon transit**
- Complement existing water Cherenkov with <1 ns timing resolution

---

## 5. Cryostat and Passive Shielding

### Current Limitation
Cryostat materials (stainless steel, titanium) contribute gamma backgrounds. Inner vessel typically dominates the non-xenon gamma budget.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Ultra-low background titanium inner vessel**
- Replace stainless steel inner cryostat with **Grade 1 titanium (ASTM B265)**, which has ~10× lower U/Th content (~1–5 ppb vs. ~10–30 ppb in SS)
- Electron-beam welded seams (no filler metal) to preserve radiopurity
- Tested by XENONnT collaboration; demonstrated ~2 ppb U/Th achievable

**Copper inner shield layer**
- Add **5–10 cm of NOSV-grade electrolytic copper** (U/Th < 0.5 ppb) between cryostat and active xenon
- Attenuates residual gamma flux from cryostat by ~×5 at 100 keV

---

## 6. Electronics and DAQ for Low-Energy Threshold

### Current Limitation
Current digitizers (e.g., CAEN V1724, 100 MHz, 14-bit) have dead time and limited dynamic range. The software trigger threshold is set conservatively to avoid noise triggers.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Fully streaming readout with zero-suppression in FPGA**
- Replace triggered DAQ with **continuous streaming at 250 MHz sampling, 16-bit dynamic range** using custom ATCA-based digitizer boards
- **FPGA-based online pulse finding** (e.g., Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGAs) with sub-photoelectron threshold detection
- Eliminates trigger dead time; enables offline threshold setting → recovers sensitivity at 1–3 keV_nr recoil energy

**Single photoelectron calibration via LED pulser**
- Embedded **UV LEDs (265 nm) fiber-coupled to each photosensor** for continuous gain calibration
- Maintain SPE resolution <15% for all channels, enabling precise S1/S2 reconstruction at lowest energies

**Low-noise charge-sensitive amplifiers for SiPMs**
- Custom **cryo-rated transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs)** with input noise <1 fA/√Hz placed near SiPM arrays inside the outer vacuum jacket (not in LXe) to minimize cable capacitance
- Use **SiGe HBT ASICs** (e.g., adapted from CMS/ATLAS designs) rated to 77–200 K operation

---

## Summary Priority Matrix

| Upgrade | Background Reduction | Threshold Improvement | Complexity | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SiPM photosensor array | High | High | High | **Critical** |
| Radon removal / cold trap | Very High | Medium | Medium | **Critical** |
| Gd-LS outer detector | High | Low | Medium | High |
| Streaming DAQ | Low | Very High | Medium | High |
| Ti cryostat + Cu shield | Medium | Low | Medium | Moderate |
| Resistive ITO field cage | Medium | Medium | Medium | Moderate |

---

## Overarching Design Philosophy

The single highest-leverage combined upgrade is **SiPMs + streaming DAQ + enhanced radon removal**, which simultaneously attacks the two fundamental limits: photon statistics at threshold and radioactive background rate. These three together could improve sensitivity by **1–2 orders of magnitude** relative to current-generation detectors (LZ, XENONnT) for low-mass WIMP searches below ~10 GeV/c².

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Xenon-Based 0νββ Detector

## Framing the Physics Requirements

Neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ) sensitivity scales approximately as:

**S ∝ a · M · t / (B · ΔE · M)^(1/2)**

So the figure of merit demands: maximize **xenon mass** and **isotopic fraction**, minimize **background index** (counts/keV/kg/yr) and **energy resolution (ΔE)**. Each upgrade below targets one or more of these.

---

## 1. Energy Resolution Improvements

### 1a. Simultaneous Charge + Light Readout with Optimized Anti-Correlation

**Current limitation:** TPC detectors (EXO-200, nEXO) use charge (ionization) and scintillation separately. Anti-correlation between the two signals can partially cancel fluctuations, but light collection efficiency (LCE) is the bottleneck.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- **Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) with ~3nm VUV-optimized coating** (e.g., tetraphenyl butadiene or *p*-terphenyl wavelength shifters) achieving >90% geometric coverage of the cathode/field-cage inner surface
- Specifically: **FBK VUV-HD SiPMs** or **Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPCs** operating at 87 K (liquid Xe temperature), which have demonstrated ~20% PDE at 175 nm
- Target: bring LCE from the ~10–15% range (nEXO baseline) toward **>50%**, reducing the relative fluctuation on the light signal by ~√(5)
- Combined charge+light energy resolution target: **σ/E < 0.5% at Q_ββ (2458 keV)**, approaching the intrinsic Fano-limited resolution

**Why this matters:** At Q_ββ, the dominant background is ²⁰⁸Tl γ-rays and ²¹⁴Bi. A 1% FWHM → 0.5% FWHM cuts the background window by 2×.

---

### 1b. Cold Electronics for Charge Readout

- **Replace room-temperature ASIC feedthroughs** with **cryogenic CMOS preamplifiers** (e.g., based on IDeF-X or CUBE ASIC architectures, adapted for LXe at ~165 K)
- Reduce equivalent noise charge (ENC) from ~500 e⁻ rms to **<100 e⁻ rms** by eliminating cable capacitance from the TPC anode to the outside
- This directly improves the charge channel's energy resolution and allows finer-pitch anode segmentation without noise penalty

---

## 2. Background Reduction — Fiducialization and Topology

### 2a. High-Granularity 3D Event Reconstruction

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Implement **crossed-wire or pixel anode** arrays with pitch ≤3 mm (vs. ~6–9 mm in current designs) using cryogenic-compatible **Au-plated Cu pixel pads on PTFE-backed PCB**
- Alternatively: **charge-induction Topmetal-II** style CMOS pixel sensors directly immersed in LXe (demonstrated at 77 K in liquid argon experiments)
- Goal: reconstruct the **two-electron tracks** from 0νββ at the mm scale to distinguish the blob topology (two Bragg peaks ~1 cm apart) from single-site γ backgrounds

**Specific target:** single-site vs. multi-site discrimination at a level where >90% of single-Compton γ events are rejected while retaining >80% of signal

---

### 2b. Ba²⁺ Ion Tagging (Single-Ion Sensing)

This is the transformative upgrade that would eliminate the irreducible ²¹³⁶Xe 2νββ background tail and virtually all γ backgrounds simultaneously.

**Proposed implementation:**
- **In-situ single barium ion fluorescence imaging** using a fiber-coupled scanning probe with a **monolayer of cryptand or crown-ether indicator molecules** (e.g., BaCheck chelator developed by UTA/NEXT collaboration)
- The Ba²⁺ daughter of ¹³⁶Xe double beta decay fluoresces distinctively when chelated, detectable at **single-ion sensitivity**
- Hardware: deploy a **fiber bundle scanning arm** with a CMOS imager (cooled CCD or scientific sCMOS) and **532 nm / 617 nm laser illumination** matched to Ba²⁺-chelate excitation/emission
- The probe tip must traverse the fiducial volume on timescales ~seconds after a candidate event trigger (requiring a motorized, LXe-compatible actuator in UHV-style ceramic/PEEK construction)

**Alternative approach for gaseous Xe (NEXT style):** electrostatic extraction of Ba²⁺ from gas phase into a **Paul trap or linear RF trap**, then confirmed by electron shelving in a **single-ion fluorescence detection** setup—demonstrated in principle by the NEXT collaboration

---

## 3. Background Reduction — Material Radiopurity

### 3a. Electroformed Copper Inner Vessel

- Replace stainless steel or titanium inner cryostat components with **underground-electroformed copper** (OFHC Cu grown in situ underground, as demonstrated at SURF for Majorana Demonstrator)
- Achieves ²³²Th and ²³⁸U contamination at **<0.1 μBq/kg**, orders of magnitude below commercial copper
- Apply to: field cage rings, charge-readout frame, and inner cryostat wall facing the active volume

### 3b. Acrylic or PTFE Inner Field Cage

- Replace any metallic field cage with **UV-transparent acrylic (PMMA) rings or PTFE** stock-machined parts, screened to **<1 μBq/kg ²²⁶Ra equivalent**
- PTFE simultaneously serves as a **diffuse VUV reflector** (reflectivity ~95% at 175 nm) improving light collection (synergy with §1a)

### 3c. Cryostat Vacuum Insulation Upgrade

- Line the **outer vacuum space** with a **1 cm Pb shield** (commercial high-purity Pb, <20 Bq/kg ²¹⁰Pb) plus **15 cm of HDPE neutron moderator** to suppress cosmogenic neutron and γ flux reaching the inner vessel without relying solely on the water shield

---

## 4. Xenon Isotopic Enrichment and Purification

### 4a. High-Enrichment ¹³⁶Xe (>90% → >99%)

- Current experiments use ~90% ¹³⁶Xe (centrifuge-enriched)
- Push to **99% ¹³⁶Xe** via a second-stage centrifuge cascade: this directly scales signal rate by ~10% and slightly reduces the ²¹³⁴Xe and ²¹³⁵Xe activation backgrounds
- **Cost-benefit:** for a 10-tonne scale detector, even 1% gain in signal efficiency vs. background reduction justifies the enrichment cost premium

### 4b. Online Xe Purification with Heated Zr Getter + Cold Trap Cascade

- Install a **continuous hot zirconium getter** (SAES PS4-MT50 or equivalent, flow-through at 400°C) in the gas-phase recirculation loop to maintain electronegative impurities (O₂, H₂O, N₂) below **0.1 ppb (O₂ equivalent)**
- Supplement with a **77 K liquid-nitrogen cold trap** to capture Kr (the critical ⁸⁵Kr β background, T₁/₂ = 10.8 yr)
- Target: **⁸⁵Kr < 0.01 μBq/kg**, requiring initial Xe stock purified to <0.1 ppt Kr/Xe followed by online removal
- Add a **dedicated ¹³⁶Xe assay port** for small Xe samples analyzed by rare gas mass spectrometry (RGMS) to monitor isotopic composition and krypton content in situ

---

## 5. Muon and Cosmogenic Background Suppression

### 5a. Active Outer Xe Veto Layer

- Instrument **100–200 kg of natural (unenriched) liquid Xe** in an annular region surrounding the enriched fiducial volume with the same SiPM arrays
- This "active veto" tags cosmogenic muon-induced neutrons and Compton-scattered γ-rays in ~4π with >99% efficiency before they deposit energy in the fiducial volume
- Requires only modest additional SiPM coverage on the outer cryostat wall and a simple coincidence veto trigger (Δt < 10 μs window)

### 5b. Muon Tracker Upgrade

- If at surface or shallow depth: add a **scintillating fiber muon tracker** (e.g., Kuraray SCSF-78 2 mm round fibers with SiPM readout) in a 2-layer X–Y configuration above and around the cryostat
- Provides muon track direction reconstruction to veto muon-induced spallation products with longer delay times (up to ~1 ms for neutron thermalization)

---

## 6. Summary Table

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Target Metric |
|---|---|---|
| VUV SiPM arrays (>50% LCE) | ΔE/E | <0.5% FWHM at Q_ββ |
| Cryogenic ASIC charge readout | ΔE/E, topology | ENC <100 e⁻ |
| Fine-pitch pixel anode (3 mm) | Topology discrimination | >90% γ rejection |
| Ba²⁺ tagging (chelator probe) | Background index | ~10⁻⁶ cts/keV/kg/yr |
| Underground electroformed Cu | Material background | <0.1 μBq/kg U/Th |
| PTFE field cage + reflector | LCE + radio-purity | Combined |
| 99% ¹³⁶Xe enrichment | Signal rate | +10% signal yield |
| Online Kr cold trap | ⁸⁵Kr background | <0.01 μBq/kg |
| Active Xe veto layer | Cosmogenic BG | >99% veto efficiency |

---

## Most Impactful Single Upgrade

**Barium tagging** is the field-defining upgrade: it would convert a background-limited search into an essentially **background-free** one, because every candidate 0νββ event could be confirmed by the presence of Ba²⁺ at the decay vertex. This eliminates 2νββ tail leakage, all γ backgrounds, and all radioactive impurity backgrounds simultaneously—making half-life sensitivity scale linearly with exposure (M·t) rather than as its square root. The SiPM+cold electronics combination is the near-term highest-leverage engineering upgrade achievable with current technology.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Germanium Detector Array for Rare Decays

## Framing the Problem

For rare decay searches (neutrinoless double beta decay, dark matter, rare nuclear decays), the primary physics figures of merit are:
- **Energy resolution** (signal/background discrimination)
- **Background rejection efficiency** (sensitivity scales with √(background))
- **Detection efficiency / active mass**
- **Low-energy threshold** (for sub-keV signals)

---

## 1. Detector Crystal Upgrades

### 1.1 Point-Contact Geometry → Inverted Coaxial Point-Contact (ICPC)
**Specific upgrade:** Replace standard BEGe or coaxial detectors with **inverted coaxial point-contact (ICPC) detectors**

- Single readout electrode (~1 mm contact) preserves sub-keV threshold capability of BEGe but in a **>1 kg crystal** (vs. ~0.9 kg BEGe limit)
- Demonstrated by LEGEND collaboration: ~2 kg ICPCs achieving FWHM ~2.5 keV at Qββ (2039 keV)
- Large detector mass reduces the detector-count-dependent contributions to background (fewer detector surfaces, fewer inter-detector gaps)
- **Concrete action:** Source crystals from RD Detector/Mirion/AMETEK with minimum 1.5 kg mass, ⌀80mm × 80mm geometry

### 1.2 Enrichment and Zone Refining
- Use **>92% enriched ⁷⁶Ge** material (vs. natural Ge for background studies)
- **Multi-pass zone refining** before crystal growth to reduce impurity concentration to <10¹⁰ atoms/cm³
- Low impurity concentration → uniform charge transport → better energy resolution
- **Specifically:** Require net impurity gradient <0.1 × 10¹⁰/cm³ across crystal length to avoid ballistic deficit from incomplete charge collection

### 1.3 Surface Passivation
- Replace conventional SiO₂ passivation with **amorphous germanium (a-Ge) contacts** on the p-type surface
- Reduces surface dead layer from ~0.3 mm → ~0.001 mm
- Critical for low-energy thresholds; also reduces alpha/beta surface backgrounds
- **Specific process:** Sputter-deposit 300 nm a-Ge at room temperature before lithium diffusion on n+ contact

---

## 2. Front-End Electronics

### 2.1 Replace Room-Temperature FETs with Cryogenic ASICs
**Specific upgrade:** Deploy **CC3 or CUBE-series cryogenic charge-sensitive preamplifier ASICs** operating at 77–120 K, co-located with detectors

- Current state-of-art: discrete J-FETs at ~120 K achieve ~100 eV FWHM electronic noise; cryogenic ASICs (e.g., the CUBE ASIC used in CDEX/LEGEND) achieve equivalent or better noise with lower power dissipation
- Reduced capacitance of short bond wire (detector → cold ASIC, <5 mm) vs. long cable run: reduces Cin from ~10 pF to ~2–3 pF
- **Quantitative impact:** Electronic noise contribution drops from ~50 eV FWHM to ~20–30 eV FWHM, directly improving energy resolution and sub-keV threshold
- **Specific component:** CUBE ASIC (developed by LBNL/MPI Munich), or commission custom 65 nm CMOS process ASIC rated for 100 K operation

### 2.2 Multi-Channel Digitizer with High Dynamic Range
- Replace shaping amplifier + ADC chains with **14–16 bit, 250 MHz flash ADCs** (e.g., CAEN V1725, or custom FADC boards)
- Enables full digital pulse-shape analysis (PSA) — critical for background rejection (see Section 4)
- Dual-gain input stages to handle both signal range and prevent saturation from high-energy backgrounds
- **Specifically:** 16-bit resolution, 250 MS/s, with anti-aliasing filter matched to Ge charge-collection timescale (~1 µs)

---

## 3. Shielding Architecture

### 3.1 Active Liquid Argon Veto → Instrumented with SiPM-Based Light Readout
**Specific upgrade:** Replace passive lead/copper shield with **instrumented liquid argon (LAr) active veto**

- LAr scintillates at 128 nm (VUV); instrument with **silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) coated with wavelength-shifting TPB (tetraphenylbutadiene)** converting 128 nm → 420 nm
- LEGEND-200 demonstrated >99.9% veto efficiency for gamma/muon backgrounds using this approach
- **Concrete design:** Tile inner LAr volume with ~1,000 Hamamatsu VUV4 SiPMs (6×6 mm²) or FBK NUV-HD-SF SiPMs, achieving >5% photon detection efficiency in LAr
- This replaces copper/lead passive shielding while simultaneously providing the cryogenic medium for detector operation
- **Background rejection factor:** ~20–50× reduction in ²⁰⁸Tl and ²¹⁴Bi gamma backgrounds entering the detector ROI

### 3.2 Electroformed Copper Inner Shield
- Machine **electroformed copper** (EFC) components for innermost structure (detector holders, signal cables, spring contacts)
- EFC has ²²⁶Ra activity <0.1 µBq/kg vs. 1–10 µBq/kg for OFHC copper
- **Specific source:** PNNL electroforming facility or equivalent; minimum 6-month deposition for 20 mm thick components
- Critical because copper within 5 cm of detectors contributes directly to continuum background near Qββ

### 3.3 Muon Veto System
- Surround the outer shield with **plastic scintillator panels** (e.g., Eljen EJ-200) + PMT readout, achieving >99.5% muon tagging efficiency
- Combine with **water Cherenkov outer layer** (8 m diameter) instrumented with 8" PMTs (e.g., Hamamatsu R5912)
- Reduces cosmogenic activation of Ge and ⁷⁷Ge production in-situ

---

## 4. Pulse-Shape Analysis Hardware Infrastructure

### 4.1 High-Bandwidth Signal Transmission
- Replace conventional coaxial cables inside the cryostat with **flat flex Kapton cables** (lower mass, lower U/Th content, ~1 pF/cm capacitance)
- Alternatively: **optical signal transmission** inside cryostat using VCSELs + optical fiber to eliminate copper conductors (eliminates thermally-conducted backgrounds, reduces EMI)

### 4.2 Hardware-Level PSA Trigger
- Implement **FPGA-based online pulse-shape discrimination** (e.g., Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+) to compute A/E (current amplitude over energy) ratio in real time
- Multi-site events (Compton scattering background) produce lower A/E; single-site events (0νββ signal) produce higher A/E
- Hardware trigger reduces data rate by ~10×, enabling larger arrays without proportional DAQ scaling
- **Specific metric target:** PSA rejection of 90% of Compton background while retaining 90% signal efficiency (demonstrated in GERDA Phase II)

---

## 5. Detector Mounting and Mechanical

### 5.1 Low-Mass, Low-Background Detector Holders
- Replace PTFE/PEEK holders (contain fluorine, potential neutron-activated backgrounds) with **silicon or ultra-pure silica** holder components
- Silicon holders: machined from detector-grade Si, U/Th < 10 ppt, no radioactive fluorine isotopes
- **Specific design:** 3-point contact silicon spring-clip design (minimizes contact area → reduced microphonic noise and dead-layer stress)

### 5.2 Detector Array Geometry Optimization
- Arrange detectors in **close-packed hexagonal string arrays** with inter-detector gap <5 mm
- Enables **detector-to-detector coincidence veto**: events depositing energy in two adjacent detectors are vetoed (Compton scattering rejection)
- Increases granularity without reducing total mass
- **Quantitative:** <5 mm gap gives >70% probability of detecting second Compton scatter in adjacent detector

---

## 6. Cryogenic Infrastructure

### 6.1 Pulse-Tube Refrigerators → Low-Vibration PTRs
- Replace liquid nitrogen/liquid argon cooling with **pulse-tube refrigerators (PTRs)** (e.g., Cryomech PT415 or Sumitomo RP-082B)
- Eliminates cryogen refills (reduces human-introduced backgrounds from access)
- **Specify low-vibration variants** (Cryomech LP series with remote valve motor) to prevent microphonic noise coupling to detector readout
- Add **vibration isolation bellows** between PTR cold head and detector suspension

### 6.2 Radon Exclusion System
- Install **radon trap** (activated charcoal at −78°C) on all gas inlets to inner shield volume
- Achieve Rn activity in inner volume <1 mBq/m³ (vs. ~10–50 Bq/m³ in lab air)
- Use **Rn-free compressed N₂ blanket** continuously flushing above LAr surface

---

## Priority Ranking by Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Impact on Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| ICPC detectors (>1.5 kg) | Mass scaling + resolution | High |
| Cryogenic ASIC preamplifiers | Energy resolution + threshold | High |
| Instrumented LAr SiPM veto | Background × ~30 reduction | Very High |
| Electroformed copper holders | Near-detector radioactivity | High |
| FPGA PSA online trigger | Background rejection | Medium-High |
| Low-vibration PTR + isolation | Noise floor / stability | Medium |
| Radon exclusion | Continuum background | Medium |

---

## Summary

The **single highest-leverage upgrade** is the combination of **ICPC detectors + instrumented LAr veto with SiPM readout**: this simultaneously increases active mass per channel and provides the most powerful background rejection handle. The second-highest-leverage upgrade is **cryogenic ASICs** co-located with detectors, which directly improves energy resolution (the primary discriminator between signal and residual background). These three together define the LEGEND-1000 approach and represent the current experimental frontier.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Xenon Dark Matter Detector

## Context: Primary Physics Performance Drivers

For a xenon TPC (like LZ, XENONnT, PandaX), primary performance metrics are:
- **Background rejection** (nuclear recoil vs. electron recoil discrimination)
- **Energy threshold** (minimum detectable recoil energy)
- **Fiducial mass** (signal efficiency per kg)
- **Self-shielding integrity** (background rate in fiducial volume)

---

## 1. Photosensor Upgrades (Highest Leverage)

### Current limitation
Standard 3" Hamamatsu R11410-23 PMTs have ~35% QE, ~50 dark count rate/cm²/s at LXe temperature, and contribute radon/radioactivity backgrounds.

### Proposed upgrades

**Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) — specifically Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) RGB-HD or Hamamatsu VUV4 series**
- QE achievable: **50–60% at 175 nm VUV**, vs. ~35% for current PMTs
- Impact: directly lowers energy threshold; at few-keV nuclear recoil, photon statistics are the limiting factor
- Single-photon resolution eliminates PMT after-pulsing artifacts that mimic S2 signals
- Mass: SiPM tiles are ~10–100× less massive per active area → lower intrinsic radioactivity per photon collected
- **Specific recommendation**: tile the cathode with 6×6 mm² VUV-sensitive SiPM arrays on low-background PTFE-mounted PCBs, replacing bottom PMT array first (S2 collection dominates threshold)

**Cryogenic amplification ASICs (e.g., BF862 JFET or custom CMOS at 170K)**
- Operate front-end electronics inside the xenon volume or immediately at flange
- Eliminates ~10 m of signal cable capacitance that degrades single-photoelectron resolution
- Target: equivalent noise charge < 100 e⁻ at the SiPM input

---

## 2. Electron Lifetime / Purity System

### Current limitation
Electron lifetime in LXe is limited by electronegative impurities (O₂, H₂O at ppb level). Below ~1 ms lifetime, S2 signals from the top of the drift volume are attenuated, raising effective threshold.

### Proposed upgrades

**Continuous hot getter recirculation — SAES PS4-MT50 or equivalent rare-gas-grade**
- Replace batch/periodic purification with **two independent recirculation loops** operating simultaneously: one gas-phase, one liquid-phase
- Liquid-phase recirculation via magnetically coupled cryogenic pump (e.g., Barber-Nichols heritage) at 5–10 LXe/hour
- Target: electron lifetime > 10 ms (vs. ~3–5 ms typical in current generation)
- Impact: enables drift fields up to 500 V/cm over 1.5 m drift without >20% S2 attenuation

**Online purity monitoring**
- Dedicated small-volume alpha source (²¹⁰Po on thin wire, ~10 Bq) in a side monitoring cell, not in fiducial volume
- Real-time electron lifetime measurement every 60 seconds
- Allows feedback control of recirculation flow rate

---

## 3. Electric Field Cage Redesign

### Current limitation
Field non-uniformity causes charge loss at TPC walls and creates position-reconstruction artifacts that reduce effective fiducial volume. Wire-grid electrodes (current standard) suffer from tension loss at cryogenic temperatures and electroluminescence from wires themselves.

### Proposed upgrades

**Photolithographically etched titanium mesh electrodes**
- Replace tensioned wire grids with **acid-etched 50 μm Ti foil meshes**, 85–90% optical transmission
- Thermal contraction matched to PTFE structure; no tension management needed at 170K
- Eliminates wire sag — field uniformity < 0.5% variation across drift volume
- Ti has low radioactivity (< 0.1 mBq/kg ²²⁶Ra achievable with material selection)

**Resistive field cage using ion-implanted silicon strips or thick-film resistors on PTFE**
- Replace copper field-shaping rings (radioactivity source) with **laser-trimmed thick-film resistors on PEEK substrate**
- Target: 10 GΩ/cm ladder, uniform to 0.1%
- Eliminates corona discharge sites that generate spurious photons mimicking S1

---

## 4. Veto Systems

### Current limitation
Neutron single-scatter mimics WIMP nuclear recoil perfectly. Current Gd-doped water Cherenkov vetoes have ~95% neutron capture efficiency but with gaps at the cryostat neck region.

### Proposed upgrades

**Gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator (Gd-LS) active veto — 0.1% Gd by mass in LAB+PPO**
- Replace pure mineral oil or water outer veto with **Gd-LS** (as pioneered in EGADS/Super-K Gd program)
- Neutron capture on ¹⁵⁷Gd releases 8 MeV gamma cascade, detected with efficiency >99.9% in 4π
- Combined with inner xenon veto, achieves neutron veto efficiency > 99.5%
- **Specific**: use 20 m³ Gd-LS surrounding cryostat, instrumented with 8" Hamamatsu R5912 PMTs at 20% coverage

**Xenon skin + gas region as active veto layer**
- Instrument the ~2 cm "skin" region between TPC PTFE reflector and cryostat wall with dedicated SiPMs
- Any energy deposition in skin in coincidence with fiducial volume event → vetoed
- Already partially implemented in LZ; upgrade: increase skin SiPM coverage to >90% with FBK tiles, reducing threshold to ~1 keV_ee in skin

---

## 5. Radon Mitigation

### Current limitation
²²²Rn (T₁/₂ = 3.8 d) emanates from detector materials and creates ²¹⁴Pb/²¹⁰Pb beta backgrounds indistinguishable from low-energy electron recoils, and ²¹⁰Po → alpha + ²⁰⁶Pb nuclear recoils near surfaces.

### Proposed upgrades

**Radon-trapping cold trap on recirculation loop**
- Activated charcoal trap cooled to −78°C (dry ice) or −100°C (cold head) on the gas recirculation line
- Radon adsorption coefficient on charcoal: ~50,000 at −100°C → effectively strips Rn from recirculating gas
- **Specific implementation**: 2 kg of Carbo-Act AC activated charcoal (radon-clean grade) in OFHC copper vessel with LN₂ Joule-Thomson cooler
- Target: < 0.1 μBq/kg Rn in LXe (vs. ~10 μBq/kg current best)

**Electropolished electroformed copper inner vessel**
- Replace stainless steel cryostat inner vessel with **electroformed copper** (< 0.5 mBq/kg ²²⁶Ra, vs. 10–50 mBq/kg for SS)
- Electropolished inner surface: Ra emanation reduced by factor ~3–5 vs. machined surface
- This is the single largest solid-angle radioactive source in most current detectors

---

## 6. Position Reconstruction & Fiducial Volume

### Current limitation
3D position reconstruction relies on S2 hit pattern on top PMT/SiPM array. Spatial resolution (~3–5 mm in x-y) limits how sharply fiducial boundary can be defined, costing ~10–15% of target mass.

### Proposed upgrades

**Increased top-array density with 3 mm pitch SiPM tiles**
- Replace 3" PMTs (~78 mm pitch) with **hexagonally tiled 6×6 mm² SiPMs at 12 mm center-to-center**
- x-y resolution improves from ~5 mm to **< 1 mm** using maximum likelihood reconstruction
- Fiducial boundary sharpens from ~3 cm to ~5 mm wall → recovers ~8% additional fiducial mass
- Enables tagging of surface events (²¹⁰Pb daughters) to < 2 mm depth

**Neural network-based position reconstruction (hardware-accelerated)**
- Deploy FPGA (Xilinx Ultrascale+ or Intel Stratix) with trained CNN for real-time position reconstruction at < 1 μs latency
- Enables online fiducial cut in trigger logic, reducing data rate by ~40%

---

## 7. Cryogenic System Stability

### Current limitation
Temperature gradients across LXe volume create convective flows that move ²²²Rn daughters and cause time-varying electron lifetime.

### Proposed upgrades

**Multi-zone pulse tube refrigerator (PTR) array**
- Replace single PTR with **3 PT420 Cryomech units** at azimuthally symmetric positions
- Active temperature control per zone: ΔT < 0.5 mK across volume
- Eliminates convective cells that carry Rn daughters into fiducial volume
- PTR preferred over Gifford-McMahon: no vibration, no sliding seals (reduces Rn emanation)

---

## Summary: Expected Performance Gains

| Upgrade | Primary Gain | Magnitude |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM array (top+bottom) | Energy threshold | 50% reduction (to ~0.5 keV_nr) |
| Ti mesh electrodes | Fiducial volume | +8–12% usable mass |
| Gd-LS veto | Neutron background | 50× reduction |
| Rn cold trap + Cu vessel | ER background | 10–100× reduction |
| Liquid-phase recirculation | Electron lifetime | 3× improvement |
| Dense SiPM top array | Position resolution | 5× improvement |

The **SiPM photosensor upgrade combined with radon reduction** would provide the largest compound improvement to the signal-to-background ratio for sub-10-GeV WIMP searches, which is where next-generation xenon detectors are most statistically limited.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Germanium Detector Array for Rare Decays

## Framing the Problem

For rare decay searches (neutrinoless double-beta decay, dark matter, rare nuclear decays), "primary physics performance" means:
- **Energy resolution** (distinguish signal from backgrounds)
- **Background rejection** (active/passive shielding, pulse shape discrimination)
- **Detection efficiency** (mass, geometry, segmentation)
- **Energy threshold** (low-mass WIMPs, solar neutrinos)

---

## 1. Detector Crystal Upgrades

### 1.1 Point-Contact Geometry (BEGe / ICPC)
- Replace coaxial detectors with **Inverted Coaxial Point Contact (ICPC)** geometry
- Single small point contact (~few mm diameter) produces strongly non-uniform weighting potential
- **Why it helps:** Dramatic improvement in pulse-shape discrimination (PSD) — single-site events (signal) vs. multi-site events (background γ-rays) separated with >90% efficiency at <1% signal sacrifice
- **Concrete spec:** ICPC crystals 1–2 kg each, p-type, B-implanted point contact, Li-diffused outer contact, operating at ~3–4 kV

### 1.2 Enriched ⁷⁶Ge Material
- Use germanium enriched to **>88% ⁷⁶Ge** (vs. natural 7.8%)
- Increases signal isotope mass by ~11× for same detector mass
- **Vendor path:** Russian URENCO-type centrifuge enrichment, then crystal growth at dedicated facilities (e.g., ORTEC, Mirion, or purpose-built)
- **Isotopic purity verification:** Secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) + gamma spectroscopy of activated samples

### 1.3 Crystal Growing Protocol for Ultra-Radiopurity
- Zone-refinement passes increased from standard ~3 to **≥8 passes** before crystal pulling
- **Specific target:** ⁶⁸Ge cosmogenic activation control — limit surface exposure time during fabrication to <30 days above ground
- Implement **underground crystal storage** in low-radon nitrogen atmosphere immediately post-production

---

## 2. Front-End Electronics Upgrades

### 2.1 Cryogenic ASICs at Detector Temperature
- Replace room-temperature JFET front-ends with **cryogenic CMOS ASICs** operating at 77–100 K, mounted directly on detector string
- Technology: **65 nm or 130 nm CMOS** processes (demonstrated radiation-hard at low temperature, e.g., as developed for ATLAS ITk or CDEX programs)
- **Why it helps:** Eliminates long cable capacitance (currently 10s–100s pF) that degrades noise; achieves equivalent noise charge (ENC) of **~50–100 electrons RMS** vs. ~200–500 e⁻ RMS for room-temperature chains
- Directly improves FWHM energy resolution at Qββ (2039 keV): from ~2.5 keV to target **<1.5 keV FWHM**

### 2.2 Charge-Sensitive Amplifier with Feedback Resistor Elimination
- Replace resistive feedback with **pulsed-reset or transistor-reset** feedback in CSA
- Eliminates Johnson noise from feedback resistor (dominant at low frequencies)
- Implement **dual-channel readout** per detector: one for energy (slow shaping, ~6 μs), one for timing/PSD (fast, ~100 ns)

### 2.3 High-Resolution ADC Chain
- Deploy **18-bit, 100 MSPS ADCs** (e.g., Texas Instruments ADS54J60 series or custom) for full waveform digitization
- Store complete 100 μs waveforms per trigger
- **Enables offline PSD algorithms:** A/E (current amplitude over energy ratio), multivariate neural network PSD trained on calibration data

---

## 3. Segmentation and Position Sensitivity

### 3.1 Electrical Segmentation of Outer Contact
- Segment lithium-diffused outer contact into **6–18 azimuthal + 2 axial segments** per crystal
- Requires low-noise multichannel readout per crystal (~20 channels)
- **Why it helps:** 3D event localization to ~5 mm; identifies multiple-interaction events (Compton background) even within one crystal; enables surface event rejection

### 3.2 Amorphous Germanium Passivation
- Replace SiO₂ or polymer groove passivation with **amorphous germanium (a-Ge) passivation layers** (~50–200 nm, RF sputtered)
- Critical for point-contact detectors: reduces surface channel leakage currents from ~10 pA to **<1 pA at 77 K**
- Directly lowers threshold and reduces low-energy noise tail contamination

---

## 4. Shielding and Background Rejection

### 4.1 Active Liquid Argon Veto (LAr Instrumentation)
- Immerse entire Ge array in **instrumented liquid argon**
- Instrument LAr with **wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibers** (tetraphenyl butadiene, TPB-coated) read out by **silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs)** — specifically Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPCs or FBK NUV-HD-Cryo series (cryogenic-qualified, low dark count rate at 87 K)
- Target LAr veto efficiency for Compton background: **>99.9%** (demonstrated in GERDA Phase II)
- Fiber geometry: ~50 m of WLS fiber per ~10 kg detector module, SiPMs at both ends

### 4.2 Copper Component Specification
- All structural copper: **electroformed copper** (EFC) grown underground
- Achieves ²¹⁰Pb contamination <0.1 μBq/kg vs. ~10–100 μBq/kg for OFHC surface copper
- Specifically: use SNOLab or LNGS underground electroforming facilities; typical deposition 10–20 μm/day, 6-month production runs

### 4.3 Radon Suppression System
- **Closed-cycle radon-free nitrogen purge** for all volumes not filled with LAr
- Use **activated charcoal radon traps** at 195 K (dry ice temperature) on all nitrogen supply lines
- Target: <1 mBq/m³ Rn in any gas volume touching detector assembly
- Nitrogen boil-off from LAr bath provides self-purging if properly managed

### 4.4 Muon Veto
- Surround with **plastic scintillator panels** (minimum 4π solid angle coverage >99.5%)
- Use **2-inch PMTs** (Hamamatsu R11780 or equivalent low-background glass) or large-area SiPM tiles
- **Water Cherenkov alternative:** If geometry allows, a 3 m water buffer doubles as neutron moderator/absorber and muon veto — preferred for deep sites

---

## 5. Mechanical and Thermal Design

### 5.1 Detector String / Module Design
- Mount detectors in **PTFE-minimized, copper-dominant** holders
- Use thin copper spring contacts rather than screws; minimize total non-Ge mass within 5 cm of detectors
- **String geometry:** Vertical strings of 5–7 crystals with 5 mm inter-crystal gap; allows LAr scintillation light collection between detectors

### 5.2 Cryostat Design
- Use **ultra-low-background electroformed copper cryostat** inner vessel rather than stainless steel
- Stainless steel contributes ~60Co and ⁶⁰Co from activation; copper avoids this
- Thin-wall design (minimize material): target <5 mm copper wall, structurally validated by FEA

### 5.3 Vibration Isolation
- Implement **pneumatic or active piezoelectric vibration isolation** for pulse-tube cooler systems (if used instead of LN₂/LAr bath cooling)
- Pulse tube coolers introduce microphonic noise at 1–2 Hz harmonics that degrades threshold
- Alternative: **Pulse tube with phase-shift tuning** + copper braid thermal decoupling between cold head and detector stage

---

## 6. Calibration System Upgrades

### 6.1 In-Situ Calibration with Deployable Sources
- **²²⁸Th source on retractable wire system** (as used in GERDA/LEGEND): deploy between strings on automated stepper motor
- Achieves energy calibration at multiple γ lines (583, 2615 keV) without opening cryostat
- Add **⁵⁷Co** sources (122 keV line) for low-energy threshold calibration

### 6.2 Optical Calibration for SiPM Gain Monitoring
- Pulsed **UV LED system** (375 nm) coupled into LAr via optical fibers for continuous SiPM gain monitoring at cryogenic temperatures
- Compensates for SiPM gain drift with temperature/voltage fluctuations

---

## Summary Priority Matrix

| Upgrade | Impact on Resolution | Background Reduction | Feasibility | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ICPC geometry + full waveform PSD | High | Very High | Demonstrated | **#1** |
| Cryogenic ASIC front-end | Very High | Medium | Near-term R&D | **#2** |
| LAr veto with VUV SiPMs | Low | Very High | Demonstrated | **#3** |
| Enriched ⁷⁶Ge + underground storage | High (signal/noise) | High | Established | **#4** |
| EFC copper structural components | Low | High | Established | **#5** |
| Outer contact segmentation | Medium | High | R&D needed | **#6** |

---

## Most Impactful Single Upgrade

If forced to choose one: **ICPC detectors with cryogenic ASIC readout and full waveform digitization.** This simultaneously improves energy resolution (better baseline noise), enables powerful pulse-shape discrimination (rejecting >90% of γ background), and provides spatial information — attacking all three primary physics performance metrics at once. LEGEND-200/1000 is pursuing exactly this path, validating the approach.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Xenon Dark Matter Detectors

## Context and Performance Hierarchy

The primary physics performance metrics are: **energy threshold, background rejection (electron recoil/nuclear recoil discrimination), fiducial mass, and sensitivity to low-mass WIMPs**. I'll address each with concrete technology proposals.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System (Highest Leverage Upgrade)

### Current Limitation
Conventional 3-inch PMTs (Hamamatsu R11410-23 series) achieve ~35% quantum efficiency and have ~1 photoelectron detection threshold. The single photon detection efficiency directly sets the energy threshold.

### Proposed Upgrades

**a) Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPFs) as PMT Replacements**
- **Specific component**: Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs or Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPC arrays (S13370 series), operated at 87 K
- **Photon detection efficiency (PDE)**: ~24% at 175 nm VUV for current VUV-optimized SiPMs vs ~35% for PMTs, BUT tile coverage can reach >90% geometric fill vs ~50% for PMT arrays
- **Net gain**: 3–4× improvement in light collection uniformity and total detected photons
- **Concrete configuration**: Tile the entire TPC barrel and endcaps with 6×6 mm² SiPM cells on PTFE-backed PCB arrays, similar to the LZ/nEXO development programs but with full coverage
- **Dark count mitigation**: Operate at 40–50 K using a two-phase system; dark count rates drop by ~10× per 10 K reduction below 77 K

**b) Transition Edge Sensors (TES) for S1 Detection in the Low-Energy Regime**
- **Specific technology**: NIST/Stanford-style Mo/Cu or Ti/Au TES arrays with ~1 eV energy resolution
- **Application**: Instrument a subset (~5%) of the cathode area with TES pixels behind VUV-transparent MgF₂ windows to resolve few-photon S1 signals
- **Threshold impact**: Could lower nuclear recoil threshold from ~5 keV_nr to sub-keV_nr for sub-GeV WIMP searches
- **Practical note**: Requires dilution refrigerator cold stages embedded in the outer cryostat — complex but demonstrated in CRESST/SuperCDMS context

**c) Wavelength-Shifting Reflectors**
- **Specific material**: Tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) evaporated on polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) reflector panels at 2–3 mg/cm² coating density
- **Alternative**: pTP (para-terphenyl) + PTFE composite for improved UV stability under long exposures
- **Improvement**: Increases effective light yield from ~8 PE/keV to ~15–18 PE/keV at 122 keV — directly improving threshold and ER/NR discrimination at low energy

---

## 2. Electric Field System (Critical for Charge Collection and Position Resolution)

### Current Limitation
Non-uniform electric fields (from wire gate grids) cause electron diffusion, attachment losses, and position-dependent S2 response, degrading fiducial volume and ER/NR discrimination.

### Proposed Upgrades

**a) Mesh Gate Electrodes Instead of Wire Grids**
- **Specific technology**: Electroformed copper or stainless steel micromesh (Micro-Mesh technology, e.g., 500 LPI woven SS mesh from Unique Wire Weaving) replacing the traditional wire gate
- **Advantage**: Eliminates the ~5 mm Runge phenomenon wire grids create at the liquid-gas interface; improves single-electron extraction efficiency from ~60% to >90%
- **Key parameter**: 304 stainless mesh, 50 µm wire diameter, 150 µm pitch, tensioned to <100 µm flatness across a 1.5 m diameter span using a titanium tensioning ring

**b) Field Cage Resistor Chain Replacement**
- **Current**: Discrete resistor chains on PTFE supports with ~1% field uniformity
- **Upgrade**: Amorphous silicon (a-Si) resistive panels on acrylic substrate forming a continuous cylindrical resistive field cage
- **Technology**: Identical approach to EXO-200's field cage evolution; resistivity ~10¹⁰–10¹¹ Ω/sq
- **Improvement**: Reduces field non-uniformity from ~5% to <0.5%, improving position reconstruction accuracy and fiducial definition by a factor of 5–10 in position uncertainty

**c) High-Voltage Feedthrough**
- **Specific upgrade**: Replace oil-insulated HV feedthroughs with custom sapphire ceramic/PTFE hermetic feedthroughs rated to −100 kV
- **Supplier technology**: Based on XENON1T vacuum CF-flange feedthroughs but redesigned for 500 V/cm drift fields in larger detectors (~6 kV total for 1.5 m drift)
- **Stability**: Eliminates the micro-discharge events that create spurious single-electron backgrounds

---

## 3. Inner Vessel and Cryostat Material Purity (Background Reduction)

### Current Limitation
Natural titanium and stainless steel contain ~µBq/kg levels of U/Th; the inner cryostat contributes the dominant gamma background at the WIMP search region.

### Proposed Upgrades

**a) Electroformed Copper Inner Vessel**
- **Specific process**: Underground electroformed copper (NOSV-grade, ~0.1 µBq/kg ²³²Th) produced at SNOLAB or Canfranc underground electroforming facilities
- **Radioactivity**: Achieves <0.1 µBq/kg U/Th, compared to ~10 µBq/kg for best commercial titanium
- **Trade-off**: Copper has lower yield strength, requiring thicker walls (~8 mm vs 3 mm Ti); mitigated by ribbed geometry
- **Mass impact**: For a 40-tonne LXe detector, this increases vessel mass by ~2 tonnes but reduces gamma background by 100×

**b) Acrylic or HDPE Neutron Moderator Liner**
- **Specific material**: Ultra-pure HDPE (radon-free, <1 ppt U/Th) cast panels, 15 cm thick, surrounding the outer cryostat
- **Purpose**: Moderate and absorb radiogenic neutrons from the cavern rock before they reach the fiducial volume
- **Supplementary**: Gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator (0.1% Gd by mass, proprietary BC-521 equivalent) filling the outer veto region for neutron capture tagging with ~94% efficiency

---

## 4. Xenon Purification and Circulation System

### Current Limitation
Electronegative impurities (O₂, H₂O, N₂) at >1 ppb levels reduce electron lifetime below 1 ms, causing S2 signal attenuation over the drift length and degrading position reconstruction.

### Proposed Upgrades

**a) Hot Zirconium Getter Upgrade**
- **Specific component**: SAES MonoTorr PS4-MT3-R-2 getter cartridges operating at 400°C, upgraded from room-temperature models
- **Flow rate**: Deploy 4 parallel units achieving 500 SLPM total flow rate (full detector mass recirculated in ~8 hours)
- **Target**: Maintain O₂-equivalent impurity below 0.1 ppb, yielding electron lifetime >5 ms for a 1.5 m drift detector

**b) Cryogenic Distillation Column for Krypton Removal**
- **Specific technology**: Packed distillation column with structured packing (Sulzer MellapakPlus 252.Y), operating at 177 K / 2.5 bar
- **Performance**: Reduces ⁸⁵Kr from natural abundance (~50 ppt Kr/Xe) to <0.01 ppt Kr/Xe
- **Basis**: Demonstrated in XENON100; upgrade involves continuous online distillation rather than batch mode, using a 10 cm diameter × 3 m packed column

**c) Radon Emanation Mitigation**
- **Upgrade**: Electropolished stainless steel gas-handling lines with <0.1 µBq/m² ²²²Rn emanation rate (achievable via surface passivation at 60°C in citric acid solution)
- **Add**: Cold trap (liquid nitrogen, 77 K) at xenon inlet to freeze out radon before injection into the TPC
- **Online monitoring**: Electrostatic radon detector (ESD) with 1 mBq/m³ sensitivity at the gas inlet/outlet for real-time monitoring

---

## 5. Veto Detector Systems

### Proposed Upgrades

**a) Instrumented Gadolinium-Doped Water Cherenkov Outer Detector**
- **Specific design**: 0.1% Gd₂(SO₄)₃ dissolved in ultrapure water (as in Super-K Gd program), viewed by 8-inch PMTs (Hamamatsu R5912 HQE) at 1 per 2 m² coverage
- **Neutron capture efficiency**: >95% for thermal neutrons, with 8 MeV gamma cascade detectable in coincidence within 30 µs
- **Improvement over current LZ/XENONnT**: Achieves ~3× better neutron veto efficiency than pure water Cherenkov

**b) Liquid Scintillator Skin Layer**
- **Specific design**: 2 cm thick LAB (linear alkylbenzene) + PPO scintillator layer between outer cryostat and inner TPC viewed by dedicated 2-inch PMT arrays
- **Purpose**: Tags Compton-scatter gammas that Compton scatter once in the LXe and once in the skin — the dominant remaining ER background

---

## 6. Data Acquisition Electronics

### Proposed Upgrades

**a) 250 MHz Flash ADCs with On-FPGA Pulse Processing**
- **Specific component**: CAEN V1730S (500 MHz, 14-bit) or custom ASIC based on the ATLAS LAr front-end ASIC design adapted for SiPM capacitance (~100 pF)
- **Why critical**: 14-bit resolution at 250 MHz enables sub-photoelectron pulse area resolution, improving S1 photon counting accuracy for few-photon signals (sub-keV threshold)
- **FPGA**: Xilinx Ultrascale+ with on-board pulse-finding to reduce data rate from ~10 GB/s raw to ~100 MB/s triggered

**b) SiPM Dedicated Cold Front-End ASIC**
- **Specific technology**: Cryogenic CMOS pre-amplifier (0.18 µm TSMC process, cold-tested to 77 K) mounted directly on the SiPM tiles
- **Key spec**: Noise equivalent charge <0.1 PE, power dissipation <1 mW per channel to avoid heat load on the cryostat
- **Heritage**: Based on LArASIC (SBND experiment) redesigned for 175 nm VUV SiPM spectral response

---

## Priority Ranking by Physics Impact

| Priority | Upgrade | Primary Metric Improved | Difficulty |
|----------|---------|------------------------|------------|
| 1 | SiPM full-coverage tiling | Threshold, uniformity | High |
| 2 | Mesh gate electrodes | S2 extraction efficiency, ER/NR discrimination | Medium |
| 3 | Electroformed copper vessel | ER background | High |
| 4 | Cryogenic distillation (online) | ⁸⁵Kr ER background | Medium |
| 5 | Gd-doped water veto | Neutron background | Medium |
| 6 | Resistive field cage | Fiducial volume definition | Medium |
| 7 | Cold front-end ASIC | Threshold, dead time | High |

---

## Summary

The single most impactful upgrade is **full-coverage SiPM tiling with VUV-optimized devices**, which simultaneously improves light yield, threshold, and spatial uniformity. Combined with **mesh gate electrodes for >90% electron extraction** and **electroformed copper for the inner vessel**, these three changes would reduce the energy threshold by ~5× and the background rate by ~100× compared to current-generation detectors, potentially enabling sensitivity to WIMP-nucleon cross sections below 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² and extending the detectable WIMP mass range below 1 GeV/c².

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Kilometre-Scale Gravitational-Wave Interferometers

## Framing the Problem

The primary figure of merit is **strain sensitivity h(f)** across the detection band (~5 Hz – 5 kHz). Noise floors are set by: quantum noise (shot + radiation pressure), thermal noise (mirror, suspension, coating), seismic/Newtonian noise, and technical noise (laser, control). I'll address each with concrete proposals.

---

## 1. Quantum Noise Reduction

### 1.1 Frequency-Dependent Squeezing via Filter Cavities

**Current state:** LIGO/Virgo inject ~15 dB broadband squeezed light, but shot noise and radiation pressure noise trade off.

**Upgrade:**
- **300 m filter cavity** (etalon with ~1 Hz linewidth) inside the vacuum system to rotate the squeezing ellipse from frequency-independent to frequency-dependent
- Mirror substrate: **fused silica, superpolished to <0.1 nm RMS**, diameter 15 cm
- Cavity finesse: ~4,000–6,000 using ion-beam-sputtered (IBS) Ta₂O₅/SiO₂ coatings with specified absorption <1 ppm
- Squeezing source: **periodically poled KTP (PPKTP) crystal** in OPO cavity, pumped at 532 nm, producing ~15 dB of squeezing at 1064 nm
- Target: simultaneous improvement across full band, ~6 dB sensitivity gain in both regimes

### 1.2 Variational Readout / Speed Meter Topology

- Implement a **Sagnac speed meter** configuration or **variational readout** using an output mode cleaner with tunable reflectivity
- Replace standard homodyne detection with **balanced homodyne + feedforward** to measure a frequency-dependent quadrature
- Required: low-loss (~0.1%) output Faraday isolators and beam-splitters in polarization-maintaining configuration

### 1.3 Increased Circulating Power

- Raise arm cavity circulating power from ~750 kW → **3–5 MW** using higher-finesse arm cavities (F ~ 1500)
- Requires: 500 W Nd:YAG or fiber-amplified master-oscillator power-amplifier (MOPA) laser
- **High-power beam splitter** with 5 cm thick fused silica substrate to manage thermal lensing
- Parametric instability mitigation: **electrostatic actuator rings** on test masses to damp acoustic modes excited above ~10 kHz

---

## 2. Thermal Noise Reduction

### 2.1 Cryogenic Test Masses

**This is the single highest-impact upgrade for mid-band (20–200 Hz) sensitivity.**

- Cool test masses to **20 K** (silicon) or **120 K** (silicon near zero-thermal-expansion point)
- **Material:** Switch from fused silica to **monocrystalline silicon** (⌀ 45 cm, 200 kg)
  - Silicon at 120 K: mechanical Q > 10⁸, thermal conductivity ~500 W/mK
  - Requires operating wavelength shift to **1550 nm** or **2000 nm** (silicon is transparent)
- Cryostat design: multi-stage pulse-tube coolers with vibration isolation; cold shields at 4 K surrounding test mass
- Heat extraction: **thermal links of high-purity aluminum or sapphire ribbons** connecting mirror to cold stage, designed to minimize mechanical loss

### 2.2 Crystalline Mirror Coatings

- Replace amorphous IBS Ta₂O₅/SiO₂ coatings (mechanical loss φ ~ 4×10⁻⁴) with **AlGaAs/GaAs epitaxial crystalline coatings**
  - Mechanical loss: φ ~ 4×10⁻⁵ (10× improvement)
  - Optical absorption: <1 ppm demonstrated at 1064 nm; requires optimization at 1550 nm
- Deposited by **molecular beam epitaxy (MBE)** on GaAs substrate then transfer-bonded to silicon test mass
- Achievable coating thermal noise reduction: **factor ~3 in amplitude**

### 2.3 Cryogenic Monolithic Suspensions

- Replace steel wire suspensions with **silicon ribbon fibers** (cross-section ~1 mm × 0.1 mm, length ~60 cm)
  - Silicon fiber dilution factor: ~10⁻⁷ (suspension thermal noise reduced to negligible level)
- Fiber attachment via **hydroxide-catalysis bonding** (same silicate chemistry proven for silica, adapted for silicon)
- Blade spring material: **Maraging steel** blades at room temperature transitioning to silicon at cryogenic stage

---

## 3. Seismic and Newtonian Noise

### 3.1 Advanced Seismic Isolation Platform

- Replace current HAM/BSC seismic isolation stacks with **6-DOF active platforms**:
  - **Compact seismometer array** (Nanometrics Trillium Compact or custom MEMS seismometers, noise floor 10⁻¹² m/√Hz at 1 Hz)
  - Hydraulic External Pre-Isolator (HEPI) replacement with **voice-coil + piezoelectric hybrid actuators**
  - Control bandwidth: DC–30 Hz with >60 dB isolation at 10 Hz
- Additional passive stage: **geometric anti-spring** (inverted pendulum + LaCoste spring) achieving ~0.01 Hz resonant frequency

### 3.2 Newtonian Noise Cancellation (NNC)

Newtonian noise dominates below ~20 Hz and cannot be shielded.

- Deploy **seismometer arrays**: 100–200 surface + borehole seismometers in ~200 m radius around each test mass
  - Borehole instruments at 5–50 m depth targeting Rayleigh wave field characterization
  - Sensors: broadband MEMS or **superconducting gravimeters** for sub-mHz – 20 Hz
- **Wiener filter** (adaptive, implemented in real-time FPGA): correlate array output → estimate Newtonian noise → subtract via test mass actuators
- Target: 10–40 dB NNC reduction at 10–20 Hz
- Site selection criterion: seismic noise < 10⁻¹⁰ m/√Hz at 10 Hz

### 3.3 Underground Facility

- Relocate to **underground site** (200–1000 m depth): factor ~10–100 reduction in surface seismic noise
- This is the design choice for **Einstein Telescope** (ET) and **KAGRA**
- Tunnel geometry: triangular 10 km configuration (ET) or L-shaped underground (practical upgrade path)
- Geology requirement: low-porosity granite or limestone, hydrogeological stability

---

## 4. Optical Topology and Arm Geometry

### 4.1 Signal Recycling Cavity Optimization

- Replace flat signal recycling mirror with **khalili cavity** (compound signal recycling) to achieve frequency-dependent signal enhancement without filter cavities
- Signal recycling mirror: **tunable transmissivity** using electro-optic modulator + polarizer in cavity fold

### 4.2 Longer Arm Cavities

- Scale arm length from 4 km → **10–40 km**: strain sensitivity scales as 1/L (amplitude)
- Practical path: **new surface site** with 20 km arms, or **repurposing existing infrastructure** with km-scale extensions
- Mirror size must scale: 60–80 cm diameter test masses to control diffraction losses

### 4.3 Dual-Recycled Fabry-Perot Michelson → Xylophone Configuration

- Operate **two co-located interferometers** tuned to different signal recycling frequencies:
  - One optimized for 10–300 Hz (BNS inspiral)
  - One optimized for 1–5 kHz (post-merger, burst)
- Share vacuum infrastructure; photon pressure from one arm acts as actuator for the other (back-action evasion)

---

## 5. Laser and Mode Quality

### 5.1 High-Power, Low-Noise Laser Source

- **Nd:YAG master oscillator** (NPRO type, ~2 W) injection-locked to **high-power Yb-fiber amplifier** chain producing 200–500 W at 1064 nm
- If transitioning to silicon: **Er:fiber MOPA system** at 1550 nm, 100–200 W with intensity noise < 10⁻⁸/√Hz at 100 Hz
- Frequency pre-stabilization: **reference cavity** with Pound-Drever-Hall locking, finesse >10⁵, ULE glass spacer thermally controlled to mK stability

### 5.2 Higher-Order Mode Suppression

- **Arm cavity mirror figure error** <0.3 nm RMS (current state-of-art ~0.5 nm)
- Install **wavefront sensors** (quadrant photodiodes + phase cameras) at each cavity mirror for real-time **thermal compensation**:
  - **CO₂ laser heating rings** to correct thermo-optic lensing in high-power operation
  - **Ring heaters** (thin-film resistive elements on mirror barrels)

---

## 6. Summary Priority Ranking

| Upgrade | Band | Expected Sensitivity Gain | Technological Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cryogenic Si test masses + AlGaAs coatings | 20–200 Hz | ×3–5 in amplitude | TRL 4–5 |
| Frequency-dependent squeezing (300 m filter cavity) | 10 Hz – 5 kHz | ×2–3 broadband | TRL 6–7 |
| Newtonian noise cancellation array | 5–20 Hz | ×3–10 | TRL 5–6 |
| Underground site | <30 Hz | ×10–100 | TRL 7 (KAGRA exists) |
| Longer arms (20–40 km) | All bands | ×2–5 | TRL 3–4 |
| Increased circulating power + variational readout | >200 Hz | ×1.5–2 | TRL 5–6 |

---

## Key Interdependencies to Respect

- Cryogenic silicon **requires** wavelength change → forces redesign of all optical coatings, photodetectors, and squeezers
- Higher circulating power **requires** parametric instability suppression and thermal compensation to be solved first
- Underground sitting is prerequisite for NNC cancellation to be cost-effective
- Crystalline coatings must achieve **<1 ppm scatter+absorption** at operating wavelength before being viable at high power

The highest-leverage single investment for a new instrument is the **cryogenic silicon test mass system with crystalline coatings**, as thermal noise currently limits sensitivity across the most astrophysically rich frequency band.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Xenon-Based 0νββ Detector

## Context: What Limits Primary Physics Performance

The figure of merit for 0νββ searches is sensitivity to the half-life, which scales as:

$$T_{1/2}^{sensitivity} \propto a \cdot \epsilon \cdot \sqrt{\frac{M \cdot t}{B \cdot \Delta E}}$$

So the primary targets are: **background index B**, **energy resolution ΔE**, **fiducial mass M**, and **detection efficiency ε**. I'll address each with concrete hardware proposals.

---

## 1. Energy Resolution Improvements

*Current state-of-art: ~1% FWHM at Qββ (2458 keV) in liquid Xe (LZ, PandaX); ~0.5% FWHM in high-pressure gaseous Xe (NEXT)*

### 1a. Electroluminescence Readout with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

**Upgrade:** Replace PMTs with **VUV-sensitive SiPMs** (e.g., Hamamatsu VUV4 or FBK VUV-HD series) tiled across tracking planes.

- SiPMs have photon detection efficiency (PDE) of ~24% at 175 nm (Xe VUV) vs. ~15–20% for bialkali PMTs
- No single-point failure mode; granular coverage enables position-dependent corrections
- **Specific component:** FBK VUV-HD3 SiPMs, 6×6 mm² cells, operated at ~77 K (LXe) or ~10 bar (HPGXe)
- Improved PDE directly reduces photoelectron statistics contribution to ΔE

### 1b. Charge Readout with Low-Noise ASICs

**Upgrade:** Replace discrete charge amplifiers with **cryogenic charge-sensitive ASICs**.

- Example: **CUBE ASIC** (developed for LEGEND/Gerda) adapted for Xe TPC wire/pixel anodes, or the **VATA64HDR16** used in NEXT
- Equivalent noise charge (ENC) < 50 e⁻ RMS achievable
- For a gaseous Xe TPC: replace wire planes with a **pixelated anode** (e.g., 3 mm pitch pixels) read by **AMIC ASICs** — eliminates diffusion-smeared track ambiguities, enables 3D topological reconstruction
- **Specific component:** Topmetal-II⁻ CMOS pixel sensor (demonstrated in gaseous TPC contexts) — direct charge collection without avalanche gain, ~15 e⁻ RMS noise

### 1c. Barium Tagging (Transformational)

**Upgrade:** **Single-ion fluorescence barium tagging** using scanning fiber bundle or scanning tunneling microscope (STM)-inspired tip.

- nEXO/NEXT-Bold approach: detect the Ba²⁺ daughter ion at the anode using **chemosensor-functionalized fibers** (e.g., coronene-based fluorescent indicators — Mong group, UT Austin)
- Alternatively: **ion trapping** — drift Ba²⁺ out of HPGXe into a RF Paul trap and perform fluorescence spectroscopy (demonstrated in vacuum; NEXT-Bata R&D)
- If realized: reduces background index by **several orders of magnitude**, effectively making it a background-free experiment
- **Current TRL:** ~4–5; fluorescent indicators demonstrated in dry Xe gas, not yet in liquid or high-pressure wet environments

---

## 2. Background Reduction

*Dominant backgrounds: ²¹⁴Bi (²³⁸U chain), ²⁰⁸Tl (²³²Th chain), 2νββ tail (in LXe), cosmogenic activation*

### 2a. Ultra-Low Background SiPM Substrates

**Upgrade:** Use **electroformed copper** or **OFHC copper** substrates for SiPM mounting boards rather than standard PCBs.

- FR4/G10 PCBs: ~10–50 mBq/kg in ²³⁸U/²³²Th — dominant internal background source
- **Electroformed copper** (e.g., PNNL process): < 0.1 μBq/kg — 2–3 orders of magnitude cleaner
- Replace all polymer-based SiPM encapsulants; use **parylene-C** conformal coating (thinner, lower mass, lower radioactivity)
- **Solder alternatives:** use indium cold-welded bonds or **gold stud bumping** to eliminate solder flux contamination

### 2b. Xe Purification and Online Recirculation

**Upgrade:** **Continuous hot zirconium getter recirculation** with **radon trap** in line.

- **SAES MonoTorr PS4-MT15** or equivalent metal getter: reduces electronegative impurities (O₂, H₂O) to < 0.1 ppb, maintaining electron lifetime > 10 ms (needed for large drift lengths)
- **Radon trap:** activated charcoal cold trap at ~−40°C in series — reduces ²²²Rn emanation from surfaces by >100×; demonstrated at BOREXINO and SNO+
- **New element:** in-line **cryogenic distillation column** (as used in EXO-200 upgrade studies) to remove ⁸⁵Kr (cosmogenic ββ background at similar Q) to < 0.01 ppt Kr/Xe level

### 2c. Active Muon Veto + Neutron Shield

**Upgrade:** Instrument the outer water/scintillator shield with **high-QE 8" PMTs** (e.g., R5912 Hamamatsu HQE series) at higher density.

- Current experiments (EXO-200, KamLAND-Zen): ~20–25% photocoverage in outer veto
- Upgrade to **30–35% coverage** with HQE PMTs achieves >99.9% muon tagging efficiency
- Add **gadolinium-loaded water or scintillator** (0.1% Gd by mass, as in Super-K EGADS) for neutron capture tagging — captures thermal neutrons within ~20 μs with 8 MeV gamma cascade, well above Qββ
- **Specific Gd compound:** Gd₂(SO₄)₃ or Gd-TMHA chelate (chemically stable in water/LS)

### 2d. Fiducial Volume Definition via Improved Position Reconstruction

**Upgrade:** **3D position reconstruction** with < 3 mm resolution to push self-shielding.

- In LXe: add **top/bottom SiPM arrays** at higher granularity (e.g., 5 mm pitch vs. current 15 mm in nEXO baseline) — enables photon arrival time-based (x,y) reconstruction with < 3 mm σ
- In HPGXe: pixelated anode directly gives (x,y); drift time gives z — no upgrade needed beyond ASIC improvement
- **Light yield improvement:** coat PTFE reflector panels with **TPB (tetraphenyl butadiene)** wavelength shifter to shift 175 nm → 420 nm (better SiPM response), increasing light collection by ~40% — already baseline in nEXO but optimize thickness to 1–2 mg/cm²

---

## 3. Fiducial Mass Scaling

### 3a. Large-Format Monolithic TPC

**Upgrade:** Move from multi-module to **single monolithic 5-tonne LXe TPC** (nEXO architecture) with:

- **Field cage:** Oxygen-free copper rings with **resistive Kapton divider strips** — avoids 1000s of discrete resistors (radioactivity) while maintaining uniform drift field
- **Cathode HV delivery:** single **custom-made HV feedthrough** (PTFE-insulated Cu rod, EXO-200 heritage) rated to −200 kV for 1.2 m drift at 400 V/cm

### 3b. ¹³⁶Xe Isotopic Enrichment

**Upgrade:** Increase **¹³⁶Xe enrichment from 90% → 95%+**.

- Done via **gas centrifuge cascades** (URENCO or Russian TENEX processes)
- 5% additional enrichment reduces 2νββ background tail and reduces non-decaying Xe mass
- **Cost-benefit:** ~$3–5M additional for 5-tonne batch but linearly increases signal rate

---

## 4. Topological Signature (HPGXe-Specific)

### 4a. High-Pressure Operation at 15–20 bar

**Upgrade:** Increase HPGXe pressure from current NEXT-100 standard (15 bar) toward **20 bar**.

- Increases target mass per volume, reduces track length to ~10–12 cm (still reconstructable)
- Requires **thicker-wall copper pressure vessel** (electroformed, background-clean) — ASME-rated at 25 bar working pressure with safety margin
- **Feedthrough redesign:** use **alumina-ceramic HV feedthroughs** (Ceramaseal or equivalent) rated to 300 kV at 25 bar

### 4b. He/Xe Gas Mixture

**Upgrade:** Use **He+Xe mixture (≥90% Xe + He buffer)** instead of pure Xe.

- He reduces diffusion of ionization tracks: transverse diffusion drops from ~10 mm/√m to ~2–3 mm/√m
- **Result:** sharper track endpoints (Bragg peaks), cleaner topological separation of 0νββ signal (two-electron track with blobs) from single-electron backgrounds
- Demonstrated in small prototypes (NEXT-DEMO++); requires validating electroluminescence yield and drift velocity at scale
- **Gas system upgrade:** additional He recirculation loop with independent getter, differential pressure control to maintain 90/10 Xe/He ratio to ±0.5%

---

## 5. Electronics and DAQ

### 5a. Triggerless DAQ with Continuous Digitization

**Upgrade:** Replace triggered DAQ with **continuous waveform digitization** at 250 MS/s, 14-bit.

- **Specific component:** **CAEN V1730** digitizers (250 MS/s, 14-bit, 16-channel) or custom FPGA-based boards (Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGA)
- Enables offline trigger optimization — no events lost to hardware trigger inefficiency
- Allows multi-trigger pileup reconstruction (critical for 2νββ background characterization)
- Requires ~50–100 TB/year storage per tonne of Xe; manageable with modern HPC

### 5b. Cryogenic Front-End for Noise Reduction

**Upgrade:** Place **first-stage preamplifiers at cryogenic temperature** (77 K for LXe, or 200 K for HPGXe cold region).

- Eliminates ~30–50 cm of signal cable from detector to warm preamplifier — reduces capacitance, reducing noise by √(C_stray)
- **Specific component:** **GaAs or SiGe HBT cryogenic op-amps** (e.g., BFP640 SiGe at 77 K, demonstrated in CDMS) — ENC < 30 e⁻ achievable vs. 150 e⁻ at room temperature
- Requires careful heat load budgeting (< 1 mW per channel to avoid cryogenic system overload)

---

## Summary Priority Table

| Upgrade | Target Parameter | Expected Gain | TRL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Barium tagging | Background B | ~10⁴× reduction | 4–5 |
| SiPM VUV-HD arrays | ΔE, efficiency | 20–30% ΔE improvement | 8–9 |
| Pixelated anode + ASIC | ΔE, topology | factor 2 in background rejection | 6–7 |
| He/Xe mixture | Topology | factor 2–3 in background rejection | 6 |
| Electroformed Cu PCBs | Background B | factor 100 in internal BG | 7–8 |
| Online Rn trap + distillation | Background B | factor 100 in Rn/Kr | 8 |
| Continuous DAQ | Efficiency, systematics | ~5–10% efficiency gain | 9 |
| Cryogenic front-end ASICs | ΔE | 30–50% noise reduction | 6–7 |

**The single highest-leverage upgrade is barium tagging**, as it decouples sensitivity from background entirely. The second tier — SiPM readout optimization, cryogenic electronics, and He/Xe mixtures — offers near-term, demonstrable gains with existing technology.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Xenon Dark Matter Detectors

## Context: Primary Physics Performance Drivers

The key figures of merit are: **energy threshold** (reach low-mass WIMPs), **background rejection** (S1/S2 discrimination, fiducialization), **energy resolution**, and **sensitivity to rare signals**. I'll address each with specific technology proposals.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System (Highest Leverage)

### Current Limitation
Existing detectors (XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T) use 3-inch Hamamatsu R11410-23 PMTs with ~35% quantum efficiency. The S1 signal at low energies (< 5 keV_nr) often yields only 1-3 detected photons, making threshold and discrimination poor.

### Proposed Upgrades

**A. Replace PMTs with vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)**
- Specific target: arrays of **FBK VUV-HD SiPMs** (Fondazione Bruno Kessler) or **Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPC S13370** series
- Achieve **~50-60% photon detection efficiency (PDE)** at 175 nm (Xe scintillation wavelength) vs. ~35% for PMTs
- Dark count rates must be suppressed by operating at **~165 K** (xenon operating temperature), which naturally reduces thermal noise by ~10⁴× vs room temperature
- Tile the entire inner surface: requires ~5,000–10,000 individual 6×6 mm² SiPMs for a tonne-scale detector
- **Impact**: doubles or triples S1 photoelectron yield; reduces threshold from ~1 keV_nr toward ~100 eV_nr range; dramatically improves nuclear/electronic recoil discrimination at low energy

**B. Wavelength-shifting reflector optimization**
- Replace current PTFE reflectors with **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) vacuum-evaporated coatings** on the SiPM faceplates at controlled thickness (~200-400 nm)
- Alternatively: **PEN (polyethylene naphthalate)** foils as structural VUV wavelength shifters with measured 70%+ shifting efficiency
- Add **specular reflector backing** (3M ESR film) behind SiPM arrays to recover photons that miss active area

---

## 2. Charge Readout / S2 Amplification

### Current Limitation
Traditional anode/gate electrodes produce S2 signals but the electroluminescence gap geometry and field uniformity limit spatial resolution and create spurious electron backgrounds.

### Proposed Upgrades

**A. Segmented charge readout with silicon pixel arrays**
- Implement **CMOS charge-sensitive pixel detectors** (analogous to developments in DUNE/LArTPC) at the anode plane
- Specifically: adapt **LePix** or **ATLAS ITk strip sensors** for cold operation; or develop custom ASICs in 65 nm CMOS process for ~165 K operation
- Pixel pitch of ~3-5 mm gives sub-cm xy reconstruction without light-based position reconstruction ambiguity
- **Impact**: reconstruct single electron clusters; improve fiducial volume definition; enable electron-train background rejection

**B. Thick Gas Electron Multiplier (THGEM) or GEM anode**
- Replace wire anode with a **THGEM fabricated on Kapton/FR4** with 0.5 mm holes, operated in the gas phase
- Amplifies single ionization electrons with gain ~10-100 before reaching readout
- Enables **single-electron S2 detection** reliably
- Eliminates electroluminescence gap non-uniformity from wire sagging
- **Caution**: requires validation of radiopurity (low U/Th content < 1 μBq/kg)

---

## 3. Electric Field Uniformity and Electrode Design

### Current Limitation
Field cage resistor chains and wire electrodes create non-uniformities >1%, causing position-dependent energy resolution and fiducialization errors. Wire electrodes are fragile and have broken in multiple experiments (XENON1T).

### Proposed Upgrades

**A. Printed/etched field cage on ultra-pure fused silica rings**
- Machine **fused silica (Suprasil-grade) rings** with evaporated titanium/gold conductive traces replacing resistor-chain field cage
- Silica has extremely low radioactivity (< 0.01 ppb U/Th achievable) and no outgassing
- Continuous resistive coating (indium tin oxide, ITO) on cylindrical silica wall provides inherently uniform field without discrete steps
- **Specific component**: ITO-coated fused silica from Heraeus Quarzglas, 4–10 Ω/sq sheet resistance tuned to drift field requirements

**B. Mesh electrodes replacing wire grids**
- Use **electroformed stainless steel or titanium meshes** (20-50 μm wire diameter, ~1 mm pitch) instead of tensioned wire grids
- Photochemically etched meshes maintain flatness < 50 μm over 1-meter diameter
- Eliminates wire tension drift at cryogenic temperature and associated high-voltage instability
- Electroformed Ni meshes from **Precision Eforming LLC** have been demonstrated in prototype TPCs

---

## 4. Cryostat and Material Radiopurity

### Current Limitation
Detector vessel materials (steel, copper) contribute gamma backgrounds. Rn emanation from surfaces dominates low-energy electronic recoil background.

### Proposed Upgrades

**A. Electroformed copper inner vessel**
- Replace stainless steel inner cryostat with **underground electroformed copper** (OFHC, grown electrolytically underground to avoid cosmogenic activation)
- Achieved U/Th < 0.1 ppt by mass in Majorana Demonstrator program
- Copper's high density provides self-shielding; excellent thermal conductivity
- **Specific process**: electroform at SURF or LNGS underground labs using techniques established for Majorana/CDMS

**B. Radon emanation reduction**
- Install **cold radon trap**: activated charcoal trap at 77 K (LN₂ cooled) on all Xe circulation lines
- Trap efficiency >99.9% demonstrated at XENON; key is making it integral and continuously operating
- All inner surfaces electropolished to Ra < 0.1 μm to reduce surface area and Rn emanation sites
- Switch PTFE components to **single-crystal sapphire** or **fused silica** for low-Rn structural elements where mechanical properties allow

---

## 5. Xe Purification and Circulation

### Current Limitation
Electronegative impurities (O₂, H₂O) at > 1 ppb level attenuate the electron drift signal, limiting fiducial volume depth.

### Proposed Upgrades

**A. High-throughput cryogenic distillation for Kr removal**
- **Krypton** (via ⁸⁵Kr beta decay) is the dominant electron recoil background
- Install a **packed-column cryogenic distillation tower** (50+ theoretical plates) capable of processing full detector volume in < 1 week
- Demonstrated at XENON: achieves Kr/Xe < 0.1 ppt (mol/mol)
- Add a second stage: **charcoal adsorption column** at 77 K for Ar removal simultaneously

**B. Oxygen/water removal: metal getter upgrade**
- Replace SAES MonoTorr with higher-capacity **SAES PS4-MT50 hot metal getter** (zirconium-alloy) rated for > 200 slpm Xe flow
- Integrate getter directly into liquid phase with submerged heat exchanger to eliminate gas-phase circulation losses
- Target electron lifetime > 10 ms (equivalent to < 0.1 ppt O₂)
- **Continuous monitoring**: install in-situ **electron lifetime monitors** (small alpha source + drift measurement) at multiple heights

---

## 6. Neutron Shielding and Veto Systems

### Current Limitation
Neutron-induced nuclear recoils are irreducible background mimicking WIMP signal. Current water Cherenkov vetoes have limited solid angle coverage and neutron capture efficiency.

### Proposed Upgrades

**A. Gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer veto**
- Replace or supplement water shield with **Gd-loaded (0.1% by mass) linear alkylbenzene (LAB) scintillator**
- Gd has neutron capture cross-section ~49,000 barns; emits ~8 MeV gamma cascade detectable with >99% efficiency
- **Specific system**: based on SNO+ or JUNO experience; requires Gd-LAB compatibility validation and light monitoring with 8-inch PMTs (R5912 Hamamatsu) on vessel walls
- Reduces single-scatter neutron background by factor ~10-50×

**B. Inner muon veto with high-QE PMTs**
- Instrument the space between outer cryostat and water tank with **R7081-100 (10-inch, high-QE) Hamamatsu PMTs** at higher density than current designs
- Target > 99.5% muon detection efficiency for cosmogenic neutron tagging

---

## 7. Data Acquisition and Trigger

### Current Limitation
Fixed-threshold hardware triggers discard sub-threshold pulses; ADC sampling rates limit S1/S2 pulse shape discrimination.

### Proposed Upgrades

**A. Triggerless continuous digitization**
- Deploy **CAEN V1730B 14-bit, 500 MSps digitizers** (or equivalent) on all channels with **continuous streaming readout**
- Eliminates trigger bias; allows offline threshold setting; recovers low-energy S1 signals
- Requires ~50 Gbps data bandwidth: use **FPGA-based online pulse finding** (Xilinx Ultrascale+) to reduce to ~1 Gbps storage rate
- Enables coincidence analysis between channels at the 2 ns level

**B. Machine learning-based pulse classification on FPGA**
- Implement trained **BDT or shallow CNN on FPGA** (Intel Arria 10) for real-time S1/S2/noise classification
- Reduces dead time; improves pile-up rejection near threshold
- Specific approach: quantized neural networks deployable in ~1 μs latency on Xilinx ZCU102

---

## Summary Priority Matrix

| Upgrade | Threshold Impact | Background Reduction | Technical Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|
| SiPM array (VUV-HD) | ★★★★★ | ★★★ | TRL 6-7 |
| ITO fused silica field cage | ★★★ | ★★★★ | TRL 5-6 |
| Gd-LAB neutron veto | ★★ | ★★★★★ | TRL 7-8 |
| Electroformed Cu vessel | ★★ | ★★★★ | TRL 7 |
| THGEM anode | ★★★★ | ★★★ | TRL 4-5 |
| Triggerless DAQ | ★★★★ | ★★★ | TRL 8 |
| Cryogenic Rn trap | ★★ | ★★★★ | TRL 7-8 |
